# Sonarr Go-port — session resumption guide

This file is the hand-off pointer between sessions. It is the **first thing a new session should read** when continuing the C#→Go port. The strategic plan lives at `~/.claude/plans/curried-discovering-meadow.md`; this file tracks where execution actually stopped.

## Stable policies

- **JSON wire-shape: byte-equal with Sonarr v3 API (Option A).** Authoritative rules + audit checklist at [JSON_CONVENTIONS.md](JSON_CONVENTIONS.md). Decided 2026-05-12 to preserve compatibility with the existing React UI, mobile clients, and *-arr ecosystem. Doc rewrite landed in slice 5.J161 (2026-05-21) — corrected the long-standing inaccuracy that originally pointed the policy in the wrong direction. C# Sonarr globally configures STJson with `DefaultIgnoreCondition = JsonIgnoreCondition.WhenWritingNull` (`src/NzbDrone.Common/Serializer/System.Text.Json/STJson.cs:27`, wired at `Startup.cs:107,113`) and Newtonsoft with `NullValueHandling.Ignore` (`Newtonsoft.Json/Json.cs:26`) — C# OMITS null properties, so Go's `omitempty` IS the correct match for nullable C# property types. Forward-guidance for new JSON-emitting types: nullable C# property (`int?`, `string?`, nullable reference, `List<T>` nullable) → `*T` / slice + `omitempty`; non-nullable C# property → value type, no `omitempty` (the zero value is what C# emits). **Known divergence — case-by-case, NOT one giant sweep (J165 rescope):** the v3 wire boundary itself is now divergence-free after J164 + J165 closed the two pointer-without-`omitempty` fields in `internal/api/v3/filesystem.go`. The remaining ~129 `*T` fields without `omitempty` are all in `internal/` (NOT `internal/api/v3/`) and split across three buckets: (a) embedded-JSON DB column shapes (series time fields, `episodefiles.MediaInfo`, etc.) where Newtonsoft on read tolerates both null + missing-key forms so the divergence affects on-disk JSON contents not user-facing wire; (b) external upstream protocol mirrors (`broadcasthenet/api.go` BTN response, `scenemappings/proxy.go` SkyHook) that should NOT auto-flip without checking what the upstream wire emits; (c) internal config / partial-update shapes not directly v3-emitted. Picking these off as feature work touches each type is preferable to one big migration. New types added going forward MUST adopt the corrected posture (see [JSON_CONVENTIONS.md](JSON_CONVENTIONS.md) audit checklist step 4) so the divergence does not widen.

## Audit Fix — Tier A close-out (2026-05-20)

External review session (separate from this porting session) produced `AUDIT_FIX_BACKLOG.md` (paired with `PORT_ACCURACY_AUDIT.md` + `TEST_QUALITY_AUDIT.md`). Tier A worked through 2026-05-20 across three slices (5.J1, 5.J2, 5.J3):

- **A.3 — CLOSED in slice 5.J1.** `PHASE_5_AUDIT.md` (snapshot 2026-05-18) prefaced with a supersession banner. Its "zero write endpoints", "error envelope drift (text/plain)", "18 download clients schema-only", and "backup restore missing" headlines are stale — verified against the current tree. Body left intact for history because its Tier 1/2/3 structure still has reusable prioritization for the remaining provider/healthcheck/read-endpoint work.

- **A.1 — REJECTED in slice 5.J1 (audit was mistaken).** The audit's "drop omitempty from 32 v3 handler files" recommendation is based on a misreading of C# behavior. C# Sonarr globally configures STJson with `DefaultIgnoreCondition = JsonIgnoreCondition.WhenWritingNull` at `src/NzbDrone.Common/Serializer/System.Text.Json/STJson.cs:27`, wired into the MVC pipeline at `Startup.cs:107,113`. C# OMITS null / nullable-reference-null properties — matching Go's `omitempty` semantic. Empirically confirmed against recorded goldens: `v3.qualityprofile.golden.json` omits `maxSize`/`id`/`name`/`quality` for unset fields; `v3.indexer.schema.golden.json` omits `helpText`/`value` for unset FieldDef fields; `v3.command.golden.json` omits `message`/`clientUserAgent`/`exception` when null. Dropping `omitempty` would have Go emit keys C# does NOT, breaking byte-equality in the opposite direction. Two narrow real concerns flagged for the next reviewer in the A.1 rejection note: `internal/api/v3/filesystem.go:23 Size int64` (C# `long` non-nullable — **CLOSED in slice 5.J164**, omitempty dropped so directory entries now emit "size":0 byte-for-byte with C#; the same file's neighbouring `LastModified *time.Time` field at :21 (C# `DateTime?` nullable) was the v3 wire-boundary's only remaining pointer-without-omitempty per a J165 re-audit and was **CLOSED in slice 5.J165** by adding omitempty so nil entries omit the key) and **the JSON_CONVENTIONS.md doc itself being inaccurate — CLOSED in slice 5.J161** (doc rewrite landed; forward-guidance now prescribes `omitempty` for nullable C# properties + records the existing-codebase no-omitempty shape as a known B.7-class divergence to be swept separately).

- **A.2 — CLOSED in slice 5.J2.** `sort.Slice → sort.SliceStable` at six tiebreaker-prone sites: `internal/customformats/calculate.go:140` (custom-format name, user-editable); `internal/healthcheck/indexer_status.go:190` + `importlist_status.go:195` + `removed_series.go:135` (case-insensitive Name/Title); `internal/healthcheck/importlist_rootfolder.go:162,179` (×2); `internal/scenemappings/service.go:505`. `backup.go:368` left for C.3 hygiene. `go test -race -count=1` green; `golangci-lint run` 0 issues.

- **A.4 — CLOSED in slice 5.J3.** `AuthenticationRequired=DisabledForLocalAddresses` localhost bypass now honored. New `host.AuthPolicy` optional interface (satisfied by `*configfile.Provider` with no wiring change); bypass applies when peer IP is loopback / IPv4-private / IPv6 link-local / unique-local / site-local. CGNAT (100.64/10) gated on `TrustCgnatIpAddresses`. `?access_token=` query param now path-gated to /signalr/* (matches the C# dual-scheme registration at `AuthenticationBuilderExtensions.cs:57-66`); REST paths reject `access_token`. New `internal/host/local_ip.go` + tests. Forms/External auth modes still unimplemented — tracked as B.9.

Go-port differences from C# original: generic [T] parameterises only the info type (string for MediaBrowser, bool for Xbmc/Plex — the C# `TQueueHost` per-class cache scoping is replaced by each provider package instantiating its own *Queue instance); no rolling-cache TTL (orchestrator owns lifecycle, entries don't survive process restarts in either port); locking graph mirrors C# exactly. internal/notifications/mediabrowser/mediabrowser.go: NEW queue field + mediaserverqueue.New[string]() in constructor; updateIfEnabled now enqueues via q.Add(settings.Host, ser, updateType) instead of synchronous update() HTTP call; OnRename routed through updateIfEnabled (was firing update() directly); ProcessQueue (was no-op) now drains the bucket and fires the /Library/Media/Updated POST per batched series — when info.Count == 1 the single accumulated UpdateType is sent, else empty (mirrors C# `:130` null-when-multi behavior so Emby decides). internal/notifications/xbmc/xbmc.go: same shape with Queue[bool] — updateAndClean enqueues; ProcessQueue drains and per-item gates on Player.GetActivePlayers when !AlwaysUpdate (the player-busy gate moved from updateAndClean to ProcessQueue to match C# `XbmcService.Update :37-47` flow), then fires VideoLibrary.Scan + VideoLibrary.Clean when CleanLibrary AND info contains true (mirrors C# `:120` `item.Info.Contains(true)`). internal/notifications/plex/plex.go: Queue[bool] (bool unused at drain time — Plex has no clean-library concept; the false marker is preserved for parity with C# `:75`); updateLibrary renamed to refreshSeries (private, fires section discovery + per-path /refresh); NEW updateIfEnabled queues; ProcessQueue drains and per-series refreshSeries; PlexTv ping still deferred per package doc. Behavioral consequence: production never previously batched these per-series refresh calls, so a 20-episode import fired 20 separate library-refresh POSTs; with B2 wired, the orchestrator's periodic ProcessQueue tick will drain them all in a single batched call (matches C# semantics for the first time). OnConnect allocates the channels, registers the connection, and immediately fires the version-handshake event (Name="version", Body=VersionMessage{Version: hostVersion}, envelope Version=nil) via the public Broadcast path so every connected client including the just-registered one sees it (mirrors C# OnConnectedAsync at :41-58 which sends to Clients.All AFTER adding to _connections). OnDisconnect closes the done signal + removes from the registry; the send channel is intentionally NOT closed (Go forbids closing a channel that may concurrently be sent to). Broadcast snapshots the connection list under RLock, releases the lock, then does a non-blocking select per connection: ctx-cancel → return ctx.Err; done-fired → drop (consumer gone); ch <- msg → enqueued; default → drop (full buffer, slow consumer). Drop semantics match the C# `Clients.All.SendAsync` fire-and-forget posture — no server-side missed-event buffer; clients reconcile via REST on reconnect. PingMessage bare keep-alive frame ({Type:6}). ReadHandshake parses + validates the first frame (json/v1 only — other protocols/versions return ErrHandshakeUnsupported). WriteHandshakeResponse emits the success/error reply. EncodeInvocation/EncodePing build the bytes for outbound server→client frames. MarshalFrame/WriteFrame/ReadFrame are the generic RS-framing helpers — MarshalFrame appends the 0x1E byte after json.Marshal output; ReadFrame consumes byte-by-byte until RS (RS can't appear inside JSON since JSON encoders escape control bytes as `\u001e`). SplitFrames is the long-polling-style helper that splits a concatenated multi-frame payload into individual JSON-object portions. internal/signalr/protocol_test.go NEW (~150 LOC): 13 tests — ReadHandshake accepts json/v1; rejects unsupported-protocol (messagepack→ErrHandshakeUnsupported), unsupported-version (json/v2→ErrHandshakeUnsupported), malformed-JSON (→ErrHandshakeMalformed), missing-RS-terminator (→ErrHandshakeMalformed via partial-read); WriteHandshakeResponse empty-success emits `{}<RS>`; error-response emits `{"error":"..."}`; EncodeInvocation wire shape (type=1, target="receiveMessage", arguments=[<envelope>], RS-terminated, argument-0 round-trips back to the SignalRMessage shape); EncodePing emits `{"type":6}<RS>`; ReadFrame strips separator + handles multi-frame streams; EOF on empty input returns io.EOF, EOF mid-frame returns io.ErrUnexpectedEOF; SplitFrames handles nil + trailing-RS edge cases. Lint clean (errorlint required `%w` for the second error in `fmt.Errorf("%w: %w", sentinel, parse-err)` — Go 1.20+ supports multiple %w in one Errorf call); go test ./... fully green. NEW DEPENDENCY: github.com/coder/websocket v1.8.14 — minimal, context-aware, stdlib-net/http-friendly WS library; chose over gorilla/websocket for the cleaner ctx API + tighter footprint. internal/signalr/transport.go NEW (~180 LOC): WebSocketHandler(hub, logger) returns the http.Handler for GET /signalr/messages — the actual SignalR wire transport that pumps the Hub's outbound message channel onto a WebSocket connection. Flow: websocket.Accept upgrades the HTTP request; SetReadLimit(64K) caps the inbound frame size (SignalR frames are small, reject 64K+ payloads); ConnID is taken from `?id=<connId>` (echoed back from negotiate) with a fresh DefaultConnectionIDGenerator fallback if missing; HandshakeTimeout (15s) enforces the SignalR-spec client-handshake deadline via context; readClientHandshake parses the first WS message + validates json/v1; on success WriteHandshakeResponse emits `{}`; on protocol/version mismatch the response carries the error string + the WS closes with StatusProtocolError; hub.OnConnect registers the connection + fires the version-handshake event to Clients.All; the outbound loop selects across (ctx.Done | conn.Done | readDone | conn.Messages | ticker.C) — each message encodes as a SignalR InvocationMessage (target="receiveMessage", args=[envelope]), Ping fires every PingInterval (15s) when idle, ws.Write any failure exits cleanly via defer hub.OnDisconnect. Inbound reader runs in a goroutine that discards every frame (Sonarr's hub has no client-callable methods) — kept alive only to surface close frames promptly. internal/signalr/protocol.go MODIFIED (~12 LOC): +parseHandshakeBytes helper that decodes ClientHandshake from a raw []byte (shared between the streaming ReadHandshake path + the WebSocket transport's pre-framed-message path). internal/signalr/transport_test.go NEW (~165 LOC): 4 tests against a real httptest.Server + real WebSocket client roundtrip — handshake-and-reply (client sends json/v1 → server replies `{}`), version-event-arrives-after-handshake (the post-handshake fan-out delivers the Invocation envelope with name="version" + body.version matching WithHostVersion), unsupported-handshake (messagepack → HandshakeResponse with error field), hub-broadcast-reaches-client (producer-side hub.Broadcast delivers an Invocation frame to the connected WS client). Semantics: first Execute() schedules a fire at now+Duration; additional Execute()s during the pending window are ABSORBED (NOT extending the window — matches the C# System.Timers.Timer.Start() no-op-when-running posture); when the timer elapses, action fires once. Pause()/Resume() stack like C# — action doesn't fire while counter>0; the QueueStatusController uses Pause/Resume around its GET handler to prevent the read from immediately retriggering a broadcast loop. Stop() releases the underlying timer for graceful shutdown — Go-port addition since the C# Timer relies on GC. Internal time.AfterFunc + sync.Mutex for thread safety; fire() runs the action WITHOUT holding the lock so the action can call back into Execute() without deadlocking (a real consumer might re-trigger on completion). Race-detector caught one bug during cleanup: runner.Client's lazy c.HTTP=http.DefaultClient initialisation at runner.go:28-29 races when concurrent Run() calls hit a nil HTTP field. Fix in the diff package (smallest blast radius) — set HTTP=http.DefaultClient explicitly when constructing both runner.Client values, sidestepping the lazy path entirely. Both clients share the same *http.Client so the underlying connection pool (and keep-alives) is shared across workers — important for nightly automation where the staging primary may have per-IP connection caps. Aggregation refactor: summary counts are computed AFTER the worker pool drains (single pass over the populated results slice) rather than incrementing shared counters during the parallel phase — avoids a sync.Mutex or atomic counters in the hot path and keeps the data flow linear. Results slice is allocated up-front at corpus length so per-index writes from disjoint goroutines (each gets a unique i) are race-free per the Go memory model. Wire-shape helper that emits the C# error envelope from Sonarr.Http/ErrorManagement/ErrorModel.cs: 5xx + non-validation 4xx as {message, description, content} JSON (camelCase via STJson.PropertyNamingPolicy.CamelCase) with omitempty on description/content matching JsonIgnoreCondition.WhenWritingNull; 400 validation responses as a JSON array of {propertyName, errorMessage, severity} FluentValidation.ValidationFailure projections. Public surface: Write(w, status, message, description, content) emits the raw envelope; WriteErr(w, r, status, err, logger) flattens an error into Message=Description=err.Error() (closest Go analog to C# Message+ToString since Go errors don't carry stack traces) AND logs at slog.Error when status>=500+logger non-nil, closing the "zero handler-side logging" gap surfaced by the Phase 5 audit; WriteValidation(w, []Failure) emits the 400 array, normalising empty severity to "error" (FluentValidation's Severity default) and nil-slice to `[]` (matches C# emitting an empty collection as `[]` rather than omitting). Convenience wrappers BadRequest/NotFound/Conflict/Internal for the common single-message error cases mirror the C# pipeline branches (ApiException→4xx ⇒ BadRequest; ModelNotFoundException ⇒ NotFound; ModelConflictException + SQLite constraint-failed-on-PUT/POST ⇒ Conflict; everything else ⇒ Internal w/ Fatal-level log). Tests (11): EmitsCSharpEnvelopeShape pins the 3-key body + status + Content-Type:application/json; OmitsNullDescriptionAndContent pins that empty description+nil content collapse to `{"message":"..."}` (proves the omitempty tags + WhenWritingNull parity); EmitsContentWhenProvided round-trips a map; WriteValidation_EmitsArrayWithDefaultSeverityError pins the array + status + default severity injection; WriteValidation_NilEmitsEmptyArray pins the nil→`[]` normalisation (NOT omitted); WriteValidation_PreservesExplicitSeverity confirms caller-supplied severity passes through unchanged; WriteErr_LogsFiveHundredsOnly pins that 500-class errors hit the logger with status+method+path+err fields and 4xx errors do NOT (client errors are noisy and not actionable for operators); WriteErr_NilLoggerSafe pins the nil-logger no-panic path (so legacy handler call-sites can migrate gradually before threading a logger through); NotFoundConflictBadRequest table-test pins all three convenience wrappers' status codes + content-type + envelope shape; Internal_DelegatesToWriteErr pins the 500+logger path with method=POST; WriteErr_EmittedShapeMatchesEnvelope confirms the body parses cleanly through the Envelope struct (so a client parsing WriteErr output gets the same shape as Write output). golangci-lint 0 issues; go test ./internal/httperr/... green; go test ./... clean (no regressions; the helper is pure and not yet used by any handler). Phase 5 fix-mission arc opened; backlog progress: 1 / ~60 slices. 5.A2 (Phase 5 fix-mission: write-path foundation) — internal/validation package. Per-field validation accumulator that produces []httperr.Failure for httperr.WriteValidation, closing the 'no FluentValidation analog' gap from the Phase 5 audit. Design choice: Go's lack of expression-level reflection makes the C# fluent `RuleFor(c => c.Name).NotEmpty()` form unwieldy (would require either string keys to reference fields OR a typed-builder generic-explosion); chose a per-field accumulator API where the caller passes propertyName as a string. Typical usage: `errs := validation.New(); errs.Required("Name", req.Name); errs.Positive("Port", req.Port); errs.Range("Priority", req.Priority, 0, 100); if !errs.OK() { httperr.WriteValidation(w, errs.Failures()); return }`. Built-in rules cover the C# FluentValidation primitives most write paths use: Required (string non-empty → mirrors .NotEmpty()), Positive (>0 → .GreaterThan(0)), NonNegative (>=0 → .GreaterThanOrEqualTo(0)), Range (inclusive min/max → .InclusiveBetween(min,max)), MaxLen (string length <= max → .MaximumLength(max)), MinLen (string length >= min → .MinimumLength(min)), Pattern (regex match → .Matches(pattern), accepts precompiled *regexp.Regexp for hot paths and treats nil regex as failure for defensive programming), Must (generic boolean predicate + custom message → .Must(predicate).WithMessage(msg) — caller supplies the message inline rather than chaining because Go's type system makes after-the-fact override clunky). Property names emit verbatim to the wire so callers pass them in the C# resource casing (typically PascalCase like 'Name', 'Port', 'RootFolderPath') for React UI field-binding parity. All builtin-rule methods return bool (true on pass) so callers can chain dependent checks: `if errs.Required("name", req.Name) { errs.MaxLen("name", req.Name, 64) }`. Error messages match the FluentValidation default strings closely: "'Name' is required.", "'Port' must be greater than 0.", "'Priority' must be between 0 and 100 (inclusive).", "The length of 'X' must be 5 characters or fewer.". Failures() returns a defensive copy (mutating the returned slice doesn't affect the accumulator — caught by TestFailures_OwnedByCaller); returns nil when OK() to let the caller's `httperr.WriteValidation(w, errs.Failures())` chain through to the normalised empty-array case. Internal itoa() helper avoids the strconv import in error-message construction (hot validation paths benefit; not a measurable optimisation but keeps the package leaf-y — only depends on internal/httperr + regexp). Until this slice, every write handler would have had to construct the ResourceBroadcaster literal manually: `&signalr.ResourceBroadcaster[T]{Broadcaster: signalr.HubBroadcaster{Hub: hub}, Name: "tag", Version: signalr.V3Version}` — three fields with version-correctness pressure at each site. Nil hub is safe — the resulting emitter short-circuits via HubBroadcaster.IsConnected and no-ops (tests + early-build handlers can pass nil without crashing). FireAndLog(logger, name, action, fn) helper: runs broadcastFn and logs failures at slog.Warn with resource+action+err structured fields when both the error and the logger are non-nil. Closes the operator-observability gap on broadcast failures that the C# pipeline glosses over (C# SignalR core swallows errors deep in the stack; Go can do better because ResourceBroadcaster returns error from Broadcast). nil logger is safe — fn still runs (broadcast happens), just the error swallowed silently — so handlers in early-build state without a threaded logger don't crash. HEAD will be new SHA after commit. ; Phase 6.H (qBittorrent bencode-hash-extraction — closes 5.G1e InfoHash deferral): new internal/downloadclients/qbittorrent/bencode.go ships a minimal BEP-3 info-hash extractor. extractInfoHash(body []byte) (string, error) walks the bencoded .torrent body byte-by-byte: top-level value MUST be a dict (top byte 'd'); each key/value pair scans the key as a length-prefixed string and the value via skipBencodeValue (recursive dispatch on the first byte: 'i' integer, 'l' list, 'd' dict, [0-9] string). When the key matches 'info', the value's byte range is recorded and sha1.Sum is computed against that exact slice — re-bencoding would corrupt the hash because BEP-3 requires dict keys sorted lexicographically and ANY byte-level deviation changes the digest. Surface: extractInfoHash + 2 sentinel errors (ErrBencodeInvalid for malformed bencode, ErrBencodeNoInfoDict for well-formed bencode that lacks the expected key — distinguishing parser failures from broken .torrent contents). Plus two internal helpers (readBencodeString + skipBencodeValue) shared between the top-level walk and the recursive value-skip. resolveInfoHash at qbittorrent.go:262 extended with a 3rd fallback rung: req.InfoHash → MagnetURL urn:btih → TorrentBody bencode extraction → error. Real-world impact: torznab indexers + torrent-file-only indexers (rarbg-style) that hand Sonarr a raw .torrent without pre-computing the InfoHash now work end-to-end — qBittorrent keys the just-added torrent by the SHA-1 of the bencoded info dict, so DownloadID stays consistent across subsequent GetItems queries. 8 new tests in bencode_test.go: SimpleFixture (3-key top dict, info contains name only — verifies hash matches sha1 of info dict bytes), NestedDictsAndListsInInfo (info has a 'files' list of dicts + a name string — exercises the recursive skipBencodeValue past lists-of-dicts), InfoNotFirstKey (info sits between 'creation date' and 'nodes' — verifies the scanner advances through integer + string + dict keys correctly), NoInfoDict (ErrBencodeNoInfoDict), EmptyBody / NotADict / MalformedStringLength / UnterminatedInteger (4 malformed-input arms). 1 new Download-level integration test: InfoHashExtractedFromBencode — passes a real bencoded TorrentBody without explicit InfoHash, asserts Download returns the SHA-1 hash uppercase. The 4 existing TorrentBody-related tests stay green (they pass explicit InfoHash, which still wins the resolveInfoHash precedence). New test helper sha1Sum(b []byte) string in download_test.go for self-consistent hash verification. Implementation note: gosec lint suppressed at sha1.Sum call sites with nolint:gosec — BEP-3 mandates SHA-1 (not a security boundary, key derivation is the BitTorrent network protocol). Download Station is the torrent + usenet client built into Synology DSM, exposing a multi-version JSON API at `/webapi/<path>.cgi` where per-API paths are discovered via SYNO.API.Info query and sessions managed via SYNO.API.Auth login → SID. `Settings` ports C# `DownloadStationSettings.cs:28-65` with Host (default "127.0.0.1") + Port (default 5000) + UseSsl + Username + Password + TvCategory + TvDirectory. `Validate` enforces Host non-empty + Port 1..65535 + TvDirectory cannot start with `/` (matches C# `^(?!/).+` negative-lookahead via inline first-char check since Go's regexp engine doesn't support lookaheads) + TvCategory matches `^\.?[-a-zA-Z]*$` (allowed chars + optional leading dot) + TvCategory and TvDirectory mutually exclusive (all matching C# `DownloadStationSettingsValidator:9-25`). `Proxy` ports the auth-flow heart of C# `DiskStationProxyBase.cs:18-271`: bootstraps from a static `infoAPI` (path=query.cgi minVersion=maxVersion=1 needsAuth=false matching C# `:28-41`); `GetAPIInfo(ctx, settings, apiName)` issues SYNO.API.Info query for the requested API + SYNO.API.Auth in one round-trip (matches C# `UpdateApiInfo` at `:209-233`) and caches the per-(host,port,apiName) result for 1h (matches C# `:230`'s `TimeSpan.FromHours(1)`); `Authenticate(ctx, settings, force)` issues login with `account=...&passwd=...&format=sid&session=DownloadStation` and version-selects (v6 when authMax >= 7 matching C# `:135`'s `MaxVersion >= 7 ? 6 : 2`); the SID caches for 6h per-(user,host,port) matching C# `:177,181,193`. New exported `APIInfo` struct with custom UnmarshalJSON that strips leading `/` and `\` from Path (mirrors C# `Path` setter at `DiskStationApiInfo.cs:20-29`). New `Response[T]` envelope + `APIError.IsSession()` (codes 105/106/107/119 match C# `:80`) + `APIError.Message(apiName)` with the 3-table lookup (auth-specific, task-specific, common) all ported verbatim from C# `DiskStationError.cs:14-49`. Three sentinel errors: `ErrUnavailable` (transport / non-2xx — matches C# `:91,94`), `ErrAuth` (SYNO.API.Auth code 400 + session-error codes — matches C# `:118`), `ErrRPC` (every other non-success — matches generic C# `:122`). `TorrentDownloadStation` Provider implements `downloadclients.Provider` end-to-end: Name="Download Station" + Protocol=Torrent + Definition + Settings accessors + GetImportItem-passthrough + RequestAction-noop + MarkItemAsImported returns ErrMarkAsImportedUnsupported + GetStatus IsLocalhost-based (host=localhost/127.0.0.1/::1 → true; OutputRootFolders deferred to the SharedFolderResolver follow-up). Freebox Download is the built-in torrent + HTTP download manager in Freebox ISP routers (free.fr) exposing a JSON-over-HTTPS API at `https://<host>:<port><ApiUrl>` with `<ApiUrl>` defaulting to `/api/v1/`. `Settings` ports C# `:36-89` with Host (default "mafreebox.freebox.fr") + Port (default 443) + UseSsl (default true) + ApiUrl (default "/api/v1/") + AppId + AppToken + DestinationDirectory + Category + RecentPriority + OlderPriority + AddPaused. `Validate` enforces Host non-empty + Port 1..65535 + ApiUrl non-empty + ApiUrl leading-slash + AppId/AppToken required + Category matches `^\.?[-a-zA-Z]*$` + Category and DestinationDirectory mutually exclusive (all matching C# `FreeboxDownloadSettingsValidator:10-33`). `Proxy` ports the HMAC-SHA1 challenge → session-token auth flow at C# `FreeboxDownloadProxy.cs:155-203` end-to-end: GET `/login` returns `{challenge, ...}`; `password = lowercase-hex(HMAC-SHA1(challenge, AppToken))` (matches C# `:180-184`'s `BitConverter.ToString(hmac.ComputeHash(buffer)).Replace("-","").ToLower()`); POST `/login/session {app_id, password}` returns `{session_token}` cached per-(host,appId,appToken) key. The session-token is replayed via `X-Fbx-App-Auth` header on subsequent authenticated calls. Algorithm tracks C# verbatim: (1) extractSharedFolder helper finds the first `/` after position 1 to isolate the SharedFolder component (matches C#:46-47 `IndexOf('/', 1)`); inputs like /data (no subpath) treat the whole input as the SharedFolder. (2) Cache lookup keyed on `<host>:<sharedFolder>` - Go-port divergence from C# which keys on `<serialNumber>:<sharedFolder>`; serialNumber would require porting the IDSMInfoProxy + SerialNumberProvider chain (~80 LOC each) which is out of scope. Host-keyed cache gives equivalent isolation across multiple Synology boxes; minor cache regression on Host reconfigs (e.g. switching between LAN and reverse-proxy URLs for the same box) acceptable given the 1h TTL. (3) Cache hit within TTL returns cached mapping; miss invokes Proxy.GetSharedFolderMapping (J120) and stores result. Errors are NOT cached so a transient API failure doesn't poison the lookup. (4) Substitute via ospath: fullPath = mapping.PhysicalPath + (input - mapping.SharedFolder); the right-hand side uses OsPath.Sub to strip the SharedFolder prefix, the result joined via OsPath.Add. Two constructor options for tests: WithSharedFolderTTL(d) overrides the cache window (0 disables); WithSharedFolderClock(now) pins the clock for TTL boundary tests. nil proxy panics at construction time (C# DI posture). Single-DELETE shape per pass with a dialect branch: EnginePostgres uses WHERE Id = ANY (SELECT ...) and double-escapes the backslash (`'_:\\%'`) because Postgres LIKE interprets `\` as the pattern-escape character; the SQLite branch uses WHERE Id IN (SELECT ...) and single-escapes (`'_:\%'`) since SQLite LIKE doesn't interpret `\` by default. Both forms ported verbatim from C# CleanupAbsolutePathMetadataFiles.cs:18-43 -- changing the escape posture would break LIKE matching on either engine, so the dialect branch is non-negotiable. Phase 5.J130 (housekeeping CleanupDownloadClientUnavailablePendingReleases port): closes the second-easiest of the six remaining unported housekeepers. Sweeps PendingReleases rows that have been parked with a transient defer-reason for >14 days -- specifically Reason in {DownloadClientUnavailable, Fallback}. The orchestrator stages these rows when no download client could accept a grab at decision time (DCU) or when queue-state was ambiguous (Fallback); both are expected to clear on the next retry tick, so a row older than 14 days almost certainly stuck because the original release is no longer recoverable. Without this sweep the row would live in the queue forever, re-evaluated every tick. Critically the Delay reason is NOT swept -- DelayProfile-driven defers are controlled by their own timer, not housekeeping. (SQLite) split in one helper. The C# tree's Postgres branch uses `Reason = ANY (@Reasons)` because Dapper expands array params that way; database/sql doesn't have an array type, so the Go form is a literal `IN ($2, $3)` / `IN (?, ?)` with positional placeholders -- behaviour is identical, same rows match. Constructor pins a `now func() time.Time` to time.Now; tests step over the 14-day TTL by seeding Added timestamps 15 days back rather than mocking the clock. Three DELETE passes, one per metadata Type the C# tree dedups: (1) Type=1 SeriesMetadata grouped by (SeriesId, Consumer), (2) Type=2 EpisodeMetadata grouped by (EpisodeFileId, Consumer), (3) Type=5 EpisodeImage grouped by (EpisodeFileId, Consumer). Type=3 (SeriesImage) and Type=4 (SeasonImage) are NOT swept -- the metadata-writers for those Types own the uniqueness invariant elsewhere and the C# housekeeper has never touched them. Per-pass shape ported verbatim: DELETE FROM MetadataFiles WHERE Id IN (SELECT MIN(Id) FROM MetadataFiles WHERE Type = ? GROUP BY <key>, Consumer HAVING COUNT(<key>) > 1). This shape deletes ONE row per duplicate group per pass -- a 3-dup group becomes 2-dup, then 1-dup, then converged. Convergence is O(max-group-size) passes which is fine for a daily housekeeping cadence; the test exercises the 2-pass case by seeding 3 Type=1 duplicates and running Clean twice. Sweeps ExtraFiles rows that point into folders the DiskScanService now excludes (extras subfolders, hidden dotfolders, OS noise like .DS_Store / Thumbs.db, ...) -- rows produced by historic disk scans that ran before the exclusion regex grew its current shape. # C# bug: the original implementation at CleanupExtraFilesInExcludedFolders.cs:30-42 has a path-comparison bug -- it filters extras as full paths (FilterPaths(series.Path, fullPaths)) but then checks membership of `Path.Combine(e.RelativePath)` (the .NET params overload called with one element returns the relative path unchanged). Since `filteredExtraFiles` contains full paths and the Contains check uses the relative form, every membership test fails -- and the gate at :32 only short-circuits when filteredExtraFiles.Count == extraFiles.Count, so the moment ONE extra is in an excluded folder, ALL extras for that series get DeleteMany-ed. The Go port fixes this by using the full path on both sides of the Contains check. The fix is intentional, documented in the package doc-comment as a deliberate divergence, and pinned by a dedicated test (TestCleanupExtraFilesExcluded_CSharpBugIsFixed) that proves only the actually-excluded extra (1 of 3) gets deleted, not all three. Sweeps MetadataFiles rows whose on-disk .jpg payload is actually an HTML error page -- residue of a metadata-source HTTP fetch that returned a 4xx/5xx body the writer happily wrote to disk as a .jpg. One-shot semantics: gated on ConfigService.CleanupMetadataImages (default true at C# ConfigService.cs:381), performs the sweep once, then writes the flag back to false so subsequent passes short-circuit at the gate -- a re-trigger requires operator intervention via the Config table. Detection algorithm ported verbatim from C# :74-91: read first 10 bytes via OpenReadStream, fail-fast if size<10, lowercase as ASCII, check for substring "html". This is a known C# limitation: responses starting with `<!DOCTYPE html>` slip through because the doctype prefix consumes bytes 0-9 before the "html" substring appears -- the Go port preserves the buggy detector verbatim since the failure mode is recoverable (the file stays, no data loss) and a smarter detector would diverge from the C# observable behaviour without a strong reason. Date+ext filter from :44-45 (LastUpdated > 2014-12-27 AND RelativePath ends with .jpg) ported as well; the cutoff pins the regression window to v2-era affected releases. J158 (audit B.6 — BroadcastheNet LastRecentTorrentId optimization, in-indexer half): closes the J156/J157 LastRecentTorrentId deferral with a tier-walk on FetchRecent. C# cite: `BroadcastheNetRequestGenerator.cs:22-40`. The Indexer struct grows a `lastRecentTorrentID int` field plus a `SetLastRecentTorrentID(int)` setter + `LastRecentTorrentID() int` getter — matches the C# property shape on the request generator (`:14`). When > 0, FetchRecent now builds a 2-tier chain via `buildRecentTiers`: TIER 1 = `{id: ">=<lastID-100>"}` (the -100 is C#'s overlap window guarding against deletions / reordering since the last sync — verbatim from `:30`), TIER 2 = `{age: "<=86400"}` 24-hour fallback. The FetchRecent loop walks tier-by-tier and short-circuits on the first tier with non-empty results — mirrors C# `IndexerPageableRequestChain.Add` (tier 1) + `.AddTier` (tier 2) semantics. When lastRecentTorrentID is ≤ 0 only the age tier fires (preserves pre-J158 behaviour verbatim — every existing FetchRecent test still passes without modification, including the rate-limit / 401 / JSON-RPC error swallow paths). The populate-from-indexerstatus half (C# `BroadcastheNet.cs:29-34` reading `_indexerStatusService.GetLastRssSyncReleaseInfo(Definition.Id).Guid` and parsing `BTN-<id>` to extract the torrent id, plus capturing the max TorrentID after each successful fetch + persisting it back into IndexerStatus.LastRssSyncReleaseInfo as a Guid-shaped ReleaseInfo) is still deferred — that requires plumbing indexerstatus.Repo into the indexer construction path and ties to a broader "capture-on-recent-fetch" persistence task that touches every indexer's adapter (B.7-class work). Until that lands, the composition root doesn't call SetLastRecentTorrentID, so the field stays zero and FetchRecent behaviour is byte-identical to J157. Go previously emitted `{"resource":null,"action":"sync"}` — a real B.7-class wire-shape divergence; new emission is `{"action":"sync"}` byte-for-byte with C#. Rewrote the `ResourceChangeMessage` doc-comment to reflect actual C# behavior (the prior `omitempty kept off so the field still emits as null, matching the C# private setter semantic` framing was inaccurate — STJson's `WhenWritingNull` applies regardless of getter/setter visibility) and updated the `ActionSync` enum comment to call out the empty-resource-key shape. Three test sites flipped from asserting `"resource":null` presence to asserting `"resource"` key absence: `internal/signalr/signalr_test.go:59-72 TestResourceChangeMessage_SyncWire`, `internal/signalr/resource_test.go:115-132 TestResourceBroadcaster_Sync_NoResource`, `cmd/sonarr/signalr_wiring_test.go:80-83 TestWireSignalRSubscribers_TagsUpdatedEventReachesClient`. No internal Go consumer decodes `ResourceChangeMessage` (confirmed via grep — emit-only type), so the wire change is safe; React/JS subscribers handle `msg.resource === undefined` (omitted) identically to `=== null` under typical falsy guards. Did NOT touch the envelope-side `SignalRMessage.Version *int json:"version"` (the handshake event emits `"version":null` for the no-resource-version case) or the `SignalRMessage.Body any json:"body"` field — those are separate B.7-class candidates flagged for a future slice (the version-handshake null-vs-omit fix needs a careful frontend audit since the React SignalR connector may key off `version === null` for handshake discrimination). C# `SignalRMessage.Version` is `int?` (nullable) per `src/NzbDrone.SignalR/SignalRMessage.cs:13` and SignalR's STJson protocol drops null properties via `WhenWritingNull` — so C# emits `{"name":"version","body":{...}}` (no envelope `version` key) on the connection-handshake event the hub fires per `MessageHub.cs:48`. Go previously emitted `{"name":"version","body":{...},"version":null}` — a second B.7-class wire-shape divergence sibling to J168's ResourceChangeMessage.Resource fix. Frontend audit (`frontend/src/Components/SignalRListener.tsx:25-33`) confirmed safe: TS interface declares `version: number | undefined` (NOT `| null`) so the omit matches the declared type; the destructure at `:98` `const { name, body, version = 0 } = message;` defaults `undefined` to 0 — the previous `null` was actually a TS-divergence, not just a wire one, since `null` would have skipped the default and produced `null < 5` (which evaluates true due to `Number(null) === 0`, accidentally working but for the wrong reason); the `name === 'version'` handler at `:340-343` reads `body.version` not envelope `version` so handshake discrimination is unaffected; resource-event handlers gated on `version < 5` continue working because resource events still emit `"version":3` (or `5`) — the `*int` pointer is non-nil for `signalr.V3Version`/`signalr.V5Version` so `omitempty` doesn't fire. Twelve field flips across four payload structs in `go/internal/notifications/webhook/payload.go`: GrabPayload, ImportPayload, ImportCompletePayload, ManualInteractionPayload each had three `string` fields (DownloadClient, DownloadClientType, DownloadID) without omitempty. C# `WebhookBase.cs:45-47` (Grab — `message.DownloadClientName` / `DownloadClientType` / `DownloadId`), `:69-71` (Download — `message.DownloadClientInfo?.Name` / `?.Type` / `message.DownloadId`), `:100-102` (ImportComplete — same DC null-conditional source), `:210-212` (ManualInteraction — same) all source from C# nullable `string` reference-type properties. The C# `?.` null-conditional propagates null when DownloadClientInfo (`message.DownloadClientInfo`) itself is null — common for manual-import grabs and manual interaction events fired before a tracked download attaches. `WebhookProxy.SendWebhook` at `WebhookProxy.cs:39` serialises via `body.ToJson()` (Newtonsoft `ToJson` extension at `src/NzbDrone.Common/Serializer/Newtonsoft.Json/Json.cs:119`) using the shared SerializerSettings configured with `NullValueHandling = NullValueHandling.Ignore` at `Json.cs:26`, dropping the three null properties from the wire body. Go-port strings default to `""` rather than null, so prior to J172 every webhook body with no DC info emitted `"downloadClient":"","downloadClientType":"","downloadId":""` — a clear wire-shape divergence relative to C#'s omit. Note that omitempty on a Go string is not formally equivalent to Newtonsoft's null-ignore (Go drops on `""`, C# drops on null but EMITS literal `""` if explicitly set to the empty string), but Sonarr's C# tree never explicitly sets these properties to `""`: they are either populated from a non-empty client name/id or left at the default null. So the omitempty flag is the correct C# parity move in practice. New `internal/notifications/webhook/payload_test.go` carries two struct-level byte-shape guards: `TestPayload_DownloadFieldsOmitWhenEmpty` (sub-tests for each of the four affected payload types, marshals a zero-DC-fields instance and asserts the three keys are absent via `strings.Contains` negation, mirrors the J170/J171 byte-level assertion style); `TestPayload_DownloadFieldsEmitWhenSet` (populates GrabPayload with Sabnzbd/Sabnzbd/ab12cd34 and asserts the three keys DO appear with their values, so omitempty doesn't accidentally suppress populated payloads). Existing webhook_test.go tests are unaffected — none of them assert presence of the DC keys, and the only event path that exercises them (BuildGrabPayload populating from `msg.DownloadClientName` etc) wasn't covered by a regression test. Phase 5.J173 (webhook ImportPayload.DeletedFiles omitempty + conditional builder set — Download bodies now omit `deletedFiles` key when OldFiles is empty/nil, byte-equal C# `if (OldFiles.Any())` guard at WebhookBase.cs:75-82). C# `BuildOnDownloadPayload` wraps the DeletedFiles assignment in `if (message.OldFiles.Any()) { payload.DeletedFiles = message.OldFiles.ConvertAll(...) }` so empty/null OldFiles leaves `WebhookImportPayload.DeletedFiles` at its `List<>` reference-type default (null); `NullValueHandling.Ignore` at `Json.cs:26` drops the key. The Go-port's prior `BuildDownloadPayload` unconditionally assigned `DeletedFiles: msg.OldFiles` so empty/nil OldFiles produced `"deletedFiles":null` (typed-nil slice) or `"deletedFiles":[]` (empty non-nil slice) — both wire divergent from C#'s omit. Critical Go subtlety: adding `omitempty` ALONE is insufficient on an `any` field because `encoding/json`'s `isEmptyValue` for `reflect.Interface` kind uses `v.IsNil()` which checks whether the interface itself has a concrete type assigned — a typed-nil slice inside an `any` field has interface type `[]*episodefiles.DeletedFile` so IsNil reports false. Verified empirically with a standalone test program: `S{F: ([]int)(nil)}` with `json:"f,omitempty"` marshals to `{"f":null}`; `S{F: []int{}}` marshals to `{"f":[]}`; only `S{F: nil}` (true nil interface) marshals to `{}`. The fix combines both halves: (1) `ImportPayload.DeletedFiles` tag flipped to `json:"deletedFiles,omitempty"`; (2) `BuildDownloadPayload` restructured from struct-literal construction to var-and-conditional-assign form — base payload built without DeletedFiles, then `if len(msg.OldFiles) > 0 { p.DeletedFiles = msg.OldFiles }`. The nil interface zero-value combined with omitempty drops the key when OldFiles is empty. Two new test functions in `internal/notifications/webhook/payload_test.go`: `TestBuildDownloadPayload_DeletedFilesOmitWhenEmpty` exercises both nil-slice and empty-non-nil-slice cases via subtests, asserting `deletedFiles` key absent in both; `TestBuildDownloadPayload_DeletedFilesEmitWhenPopulated` confirms a single-entry OldFiles produces the key. The companion struct-level doc-comment refresh on ImportPayload (~10 lines) records the Go interface-IsNil subtlety so future contributors don't try to fix similar cases with omitempty alone. Gates: `go test ./...` green at 144 packages, `golangci-lint run ./...` 0 issues, `go test -count=1 ./test/contract/hostbootstrap/...` force-rerun clean. Phase 5.J174 (signalr.SignalRMessage.Body defensive omitempty — codifies STJson WhenWritingNull forward-guidance posture for the envelope body field, no behaviour change in practice). The C# `SignalRMessage.Body` field at `src/NzbDrone.SignalR/SignalRMessage.cs:7` is typed `object` (reference type, default null). The SignalR pipeline serializes envelopes via STJson configured in `src/NzbDrone.Host/Startup.cs:219-223` (`services.AddSignalR().AddJsonProtocol(o => o.PayloadSerializerOptions = STJson.GetSerializerSettings())`), which sets `DefaultIgnoreCondition = JsonIgnoreCondition.WhenWritingNull` at `STJson.cs:27` — so a null Body would be OMITTED from the wire body, not emitted as `"body":null`. In practice neither the C# tree nor the Go-port ever broadcasts a SignalRMessage with null Body: the handshake at `MessageHub.cs:48-55` assigns a fresh `new { Version = BuildInfo.Version.ToString() }` anonymous object; every resource broadcast goes through `RestControllerWithSignalR.BroadcastResourceChange` / the Go-port's [ResourceBroadcaster] which always passes a non-nil `ResourceChangeMessage[T]`. The `any` field on the Go-port struct was therefore behaviorally indistinguishable from a `,omitempty`-tagged one in real usage — but the explicit tag flip closes the JSON_CONVENTIONS.md three-bucket framing for the signalr envelope (no remaining nullable C# property without omitempty parity on `internal/signalr/signalr.go`), matches the J168/J169 pattern that flipped sibling nullable fields (Resource + Version), and prevents a future Body-emitting path from accidentally regressing to `"body":null`. The companion doc-comment refresh on SignalRMessage adds a paragraph explaining (1) the C# WhenWritingNull mechanism, (2) the no-behaviour-change-in-practice nature of the flip, (3) the Go subtlety that omitempty only covers the TRUE nil-interface case — a typed-nil value placed in an `any` field (e.g. `var p *T; var b any = p` where `p == nil`) still marshals as `null` because `reflect.Interface.IsNil()` reports false when the interface carries any concrete type (this was the J173 lesson, reaffirmed here for the signalr-side reader). New `TestSignalRMessage_NilBodyOmits` in `internal/signalr/signalr_test.go` exercises the true nil-interface case and asserts the `body` key is absent via `strings.Contains` negation, mirroring the J168/J169/J170 byte-shape assertion style. Existing handshake/resource/sync tests continue passing unchanged because their Body fields are non-nil. The shared mutex reuse is deliberate: an RSS-sync write and a concurrent RecordFailure both perform read-modify-write across the same row, and without the lock the failure path could clobber the new LastRssSyncReleaseInfo (or vice versa) — the C# `_syncRoot` lock covers the whole row, so we do too. Non-positive providerID is a no-op on both methods, matching the existing guard pattern on the back-off recorders. Why blank imports rather than a per-package reference: every concrete provider follows the same self-registration pattern (an `init()` block in each concrete package calls `MustRegister` against the per-family `Default()` singleton). Go only runs init() blocks for packages whose symbols are actually referenced in the link graph — and the cmd/sonarr binary doesn't reach any per-provider symbols directly (everything flows through the Registry + Factory abstractions in `internal/importlists.Factory` / `internal/notifications.Factory`), so without these blank imports the registries are empty at runtime even though every Constructor is implemented and tested across earlier Phase 5 slices. The notifications family had the same dormant state since the Phase 4 notifications-family arc — every concrete notifier was implemented + tested but production never saw any of them populated; J184 fixes both halves together since the import-form is identical and the runtime cost is a one-time per-package init() at boot (under 1 ms total measured). Indexers and download-clients DON'T need blank-imports because their wiring layers (`cmd/sonarr/indexersearch_wiring.go` and `cmd/sonarr/downloadclients_lister.go`) already type-reference each concrete package directly — every Implementation switch arm forces the package into the link graph as a side effect. Notifications + import-lists are the two families that exclusively go through their Registry + Factory facade and need explicit blank-import activation. The asserts are minimum-bound rather than exact because the per-name audit lives in each provider package's own _test.go (every concrete provider verifies its registration directly); the cmd/sonarr smoke test guards only the cross-cutting concern that the blank-imports collectively activate the expected total count. Adding a new provider then requires both touch-points: (1) the provider package's MustRegister + own test (well-trodden path); (2) bumping the bound + the blank-import in provider_imports.go. ## Phase status

### Phase 2 — Domain core ⏳ in progress

#### 2.0 — Parser title normalisers ✅ shipped (2026-05-03)

First Phase 2 commit. `internal/parser` ports the title-normalisation primitives the rest of `Parser.cs` builds on.

The strategic plan's Phase 2 directive: "Port src/NzbDrone.Core.Test/ParserTests/** as table-driven Go tests *first*; they're the spec." This commit ports two of the smaller fixtures verbatim:

- `NormalizeSeriesTitleFixture.cs` (33 cases across 8 [Test]/[TestCase] methods) → `TestCleanSeriesTitle*` table-driven tests.
- `NormalizeEpisodeTitleFixture.cs` (6 cases) → `TestNormalizeEpisodeTitle`.

Implementation surface:

- `parser.CleanSeriesTitle(title) string` — the canonical search-key form: replace digits-followed-by-`%` with `<digits>percent`, strip middle-of-string common words (`a / à / an / the / and / or / of`) when bordered by non-word boundaries on both sides AND not at string start/end, strip remaining non-word characters and underscores, lowercase, RemoveDiacritics. Pure-numeric input passes through unchanged.
- `parser.NormalizeEpisodeTitle(title) string` — extracts the inner episode title from a `S<N>E00.*` or `S<N>.Special.*` release name when matched, then strips `(N)`-trailing parts and punctuation, collapses whitespace, lowercases.
- `parser.NormalizeTitle(title) string` — looser title-matching variant that strips punctuation, leading articles, and collapses whitespace.
- `parser.RemoveDiacritics(s) string` — NFKD + combining-mark strip plus a hand-curated lookup table for Latin extension characters that don't decompose under NFKD (`ð → d`, `þ → th`, `æ → ae`, `ø → o`, `ß → ss`, `ł → l`, `đ → d`, `œ → oe`, plus capitalised and `Ð`/`Ø` variants). Mirrors the `Diacritical` NuGet package the C# tree calls into. The `Ríkið` → `rikid` test case exercises the lookup table; without it, the bare NFKD pass would leave `ð` intact.

Notable RE2 reformulations vs the C# regex literals:

- `(?<=\b\d+)%` → `\b(\d+)%` with capture-and-emit replacement. RE2 has no lookbehind; pulling the digits into a capture group preserves the same matched bytes and emits them back via `${1}percent`.
- The complex `NormalizeRegex` `((?:\b|_)(?<!^)([aà](?!$)|an|the|and|or|of)(?!$)(?:\b|_))|\W|_` was split: the alternation's first arm (with `(?<!^)` / `(?!$)` lookarounds) is reformulated as `stripMiddleCommonWords`, a hand-coded scan that walks bytes, applies position checks directly, and respects multi-byte UTF-8 boundary semantics. The `\W|_` arm becomes `[^\p{L}\p{N}]` to match C#'s Unicode-aware `\W` (Go's default `\W` is ASCII-only; using `\W|_` directly would incorrectly strip non-ASCII letters like `à` and `í`).

What's deliberately deferred to subsequent Phase 2 commits: `ParseTitle` (the main entry point), the 104-element `ReportTitleRegex[]` array (the heavy lifting), `QualityParser`, `LanguageParser`, `ReleaseGroupParser`, `SceneChecker`. Each owes its corresponding `*Fixture.cs` test as the first commit, then the implementation. The 1,585 [TestCase] rows under `ParserTests/` are the spec — see `analysis/parser/regex-corpus.md` for the porter's checklist.

#### 2.1 — Language registry + IsoLanguages lookup ✅ shipped (2026-05-03)

`internal/language` ports three colocated concerns from the C# tree:

- `NzbDrone.Core.Languages.Language` — 52 named languages plus `Unknown` (Id=0) and `Original` (Id=-2). IDs are frozen because they're persisted in user databases (qualityprofiles, releaseprofiles, customformats); renumbering would corrupt rows. Order in source mirrors `Language.cs:73-126` so a future drift against the C# tree is line-aligned.
- `NzbDrone.Core.Parser.IsoLanguages` — registry of 53 ISO entries (53 not 52: Norwegian appears twice, with both `no` and `nb` two-letter codes; Dutch appears twice, once for the Dutch language and once for Flemish — by-design duplicates the C# HashSet preserves). Plus `AlternateIsoCodeMappings` for legacy codes (`cze` → Czech, `dut` → Dutch, `mac` → Macedonian, `rum` → Romanian, `yue`/`zhtw` → Chinese).
- `NzbDrone.Core.Organizer.FileNameBuilder.Iso639BTMap` — 21-entry bibliographic-vs-terminological code map (`geo → kat`, `cze → ces`, `ger → deu`, etc.). Colocated here rather than under `internal/organizer` because the data belongs with the language registry.

Public surface:

- `language.Language` value type with `ID` + `Name`. Comparable by value.
- Predefined `language.English`, `language.Czech`, etc. as package-level vars.
- `language.FindByID(id) (Language, bool)` — Id 0 always resolves to `Unknown` matching C# `Language.cs:196`.
- `language.FindByName(name) (Language, bool)` — case-insensitive match.
- `language.All() []Language` — fresh copy of the registry in registration order.
- `language.Iso{TwoLetter, Country, ThreeLetter, Language}` value type plus `CountryLower()` helper.
- `language.FindIso(isoCode) (Iso, bool)` — full algorithm parity with `IsoLanguages.Find` at `IsoLanguages.cs:78-113`. 2-letter, 3-letter, country-suffixed, alternate-code, and bibliographic-mapped paths all exercised by tests.
- `language.GetIso(language) (Iso, bool)` — first Iso whose Language matches.
- `language.FindIsoByName(name) (Iso, bool)` — case-insensitive name lookup.

Test corpus: 12 tests / ~30 cases. Direct ports of `IsoLanguagesFixture.cs` cases (English / unknown / Portuguese / de-AU / cze / Urdu / Romansh / Georgian — the last exercising both the alternate-mapping path and the iso639BTMap), plus Language-specific tests (FindByID, FindByName, registry size, frozen-Id pins). All green; lint clean.

C# behavioural quirks preserved verbatim: `AlternateIsoCodeMappings` uses the original `isoCode` (not the lowercased langCode), so `CZE` does NOT match `cze` — flagged in the FindIso doc comment.

#### 2.3 — Revision + QualityModel + persisted JSON wire format ✅ shipped (2026-05-03)

Companion to the registry: the persistable composite that wraps a Quality with its proper/repack metadata.

- `quality.Revision` — `Version` (proper iteration, defaults to 1) + `Real` (REAL.PROPER count) + `IsRepack` flag. `Compare` ranks Real first then Version (matches `Revision.cs:33-56`); `Equal` is structural over `(Version, Real)` only — IsRepack is intentionally NOT part of equality, mirroring the C# behaviour. `String` emits `v<Version>` plus optional ` Real:<Real>` suffix.
- `quality.DetectionSource` int enum: Unknown / Name / Extension / MediaInfo. Used to track HOW a quality call was derived during parsing (filename inference vs file-extension lookup vs MediaInfo probe). Persisted-form is `[JsonIgnore]` so these fields don't round-trip through serialisation.
- `quality.Model` — Quality + Revision + 3 DetectionSource tags. `Compare` ranks via `QualityWeight` (the static C# `DefaultQualityDefinitions.Weight`) first, falling through to Revision. `Equal` compares Quality + Revision only.
- `quality.QualityWeight(q) int` — static weights from `Quality.DefaultQualityDefinitions` at `Quality.cs:158-179`. Used by `Model.Compare`. Several qualities intentionally tie (WEBRip720p and WEBDL720p both Weight=10) so the upgrade path doesn't keep flipping between visually-equivalent sources.

JSON wire-format parity (per `analysis/embedded-docs/catalogue.md` § QualityModel):

```
{"quality": 7, "revision": {"version":1,"real":0,"isRepack":false}}
```

Note `quality` is the BARE int Id, not the full Quality object — the C# tree applies a per-container `QualityIntConverter` to reduce Quality to its Id on serialise. The Go port replicates this via custom `MarshalJSON` / `UnmarshalJSON` on `Model` that go through the registry. Unknown legacy Ids (e.g. 11, the retired `HDTV480p`) deserialise to `Quality.Unknown` rather than erroring — preserves byte-equivalence on legacy rows.

REST-shape full-form Quality JSON is partially covered: the struct has camelCase tags for `id` / `name` / `source` / `resolution`, but `source` currently marshals as the int enum value rather than the C# `JsonStringEnumConverter` camelCase string ("television" etc.). Phase 5 swaps the marshaller when REST endpoints land. Phase 2 storage path uses int-reduction so this gap doesn't block.

10 tests: Revision default + Compare + Equal-ignores-IsRepack + String table; Model default + String + Compare + Equal-ignores-DetectionSource; persisted JSON shape pin (`{"quality":7,...}`); JSON round-trip with DetectionSource fields hidden; legacy unknown-Id falls back to Unknown; QualityWeight pin.

#### 2.4 — ParseRevision (PROPER / REPACK / vN / REAL detection) ✅ shipped (2026-05-03)

First slice of `QualityParser` ported. The four-regex revision-detection block at `QualityParser.cs:675-708` is small, isolated, and testable on its own — making it a good standalone commit before tackling source / resolution / codec parsing in subsequent passes.

`quality.ParseRevision(name) Revision` exactly mirrors the C# logic:

1. Trim the name; build `normalized = name.Replace('_', ' ').Trim()` so underscore-separated release names match the same regexes.
2. `versionRe` (5-branch alternation `\dv\d`, `[vN]`, `repackN`, `reripN`, `1080p vN`) extracts an explicit version tag from `normalized`.
3. `properRe` (`\bproper\b`, case-insensitive) bumps Version to `captured+1` if a v-tag was matched, else to 2.
4. `repackRe` (`\b(repack\d?|rerip\d?)\b`) does the same bump and sets `IsRepack=true`.
5. `realRe` (`\bREAL\b`, case-SENSITIVE — preserves the C# omission of `IgnoreCase`) is matched against the ORIGINAL (un-normalised) name; the match count becomes `Revision.Real`. The C# tree carries a TODO at `QualityParser.cs:700-701` flagging this as over-eager; preserved verbatim.

RE2 reformulation note: the C# `VersionRegex` uses 5 duplicate `(?<version>\d)` named groups — RE2 rejects duplicate names. The Go port renames each branch to `v1`..`v5` and scans for the first non-empty after a single match call; leftmost-match semantics are preserved by Go's RE2 engine, so the captured digit is the same as the C# original on every input.

6 tests covering: REPACK / RERIP / PROPER from `should_be_able_to_parse_repack` fixture (6 cases verbatim); anime `[v2]` tag from `should_be_able_to_parse_anime_version`; default v1 on a plain name; case-sensitive REAL (1 match, 2 matches counted, lowercase ignored, titlecase ignored); PROPER+vN combine to bump beyond captured (e.g. `[v2]+PROPER → 3`); underscore→space normalisation lets PROPER and REPACK match across `Series_Title_PROPER` shapes.

What's deferred: the rest of `QualityParser` — `SourceRegex` / `CodecRegex` / `RawHDRegex` / `RemuxRegex` / `OtherSourceRegex` / `AnimeBlurayRegex` / `AnimeWebDlRegex` / `MPEG2Regex` / `HighDefPdtvRegex` plus the per-source decision matrix at `ParseQualityName`. Each subsequent commit will port a focused slice with its corresponding `should_parse_X_quality` cases from the 522-line fixture.

#### 2.5 — ParseResolution ✅ shipped (2026-05-03)

Second slice of `QualityParser`. Resolution detection from a release name; mirrors `QualityParser.ParseResolution` at `QualityParser.cs:600-651` plus the `ResolutionRegex` and `AlternativeResolutionRegex` declarations.

`quality.ParseResolution(name) Resolution` returns one of `ResolutionUnknown` / 360p / 480p / 540p / 576p / 720p / 1080p / 2160p:

1. Match `ResolutionRegex` (the main 7-branch alternation: `360p`, `480p|480i|640x480|848x480`, `540p`, `576p`, `720p|1280x720|960p`, `1080p|1920x1080|1440p|FHD|1080i|4kto1080p`, `2160p|3840x2160|4k[-_. ](?:UHD|HEVC|BD|H265)|(?:UHD|HEVC|BD|H265)[-_. ]4k`). Each branch has a UNIQUE group name; RE2 compiles directly with no rewrite.
2. Fallback to `AlternativeResolutionRegex` (`UHD` or `[4K]`) — a match implies 2160p. The C# original uses two `(?<R2160p>...)` groups with the SAME name; RE2 rejects duplicates so the Go port elides the names since both branches map to the same Resolution.
3. Otherwise `ResolutionUnknown`.

Group-priority order (R360p → R2160p) is preserved through a small lookup table; SubexpIndex is precomputed at package init so the hot path doesn't pay the lookup cost.

3 tests / ~30 cases: ParseResolution table covering every spelling per resolution drawn from `should_parse_*_quality` fixtures (`[480p]`, `848x480`, `1280x720`, `1920x1080`, `1080i`, `FHD`, `1440p`, `3840x2160`); UHD / [4K] alternative-path cases; leftmost-match-wins behaviour with overlapping tags; `4k UHD` / `UHD 4k` / `4k HEVC` patterns inside the R2160p branch (not via the alternative path); empty / no-resolution → Unknown.

#### 2.6 — ParseCodec + IsRemux ✅ shipped (2026-05-03)

Third and fourth slices of `QualityParser`. Two small, RE2-clean regex helpers feeding the still-unported `ParseQualityName` decision matrix. Each is independently testable on the same shape as 2.4/2.5 (regex slice → tests-first → implementation); `ParseQualityName` itself remains deferred to a later commit once all the input regexes are ported.

`quality.ParseCodec(name) Codec` — the 5-branch CodecRegex from `QualityParser.cs:56`. Returns `CodecUnknown` / `CodecX264` / `CodecH264` / `CodecXvidHD` / `CodecXvid` / `CodecDivX`. Each branch has a UNIQUE group name (the regex compiles directly under RE2 with no rewrite); branch ORDER pins XvidHD before Xvid so the longer token wins on leftmost match. Group-priority lookup table + precomputed SubexpIndex mirrors the ParseResolution shape.

The C# code does not expose a public `ParseCodec` method — the regex is consumed inline at `QualityParser.cs:117` via `codecRegex.Groups["xvid"].Success` etc. Exposing a typed `Codec` value here keeps the regex slice testable on its own and gives `ParseQualityName` a single call site to consume when it lands.

`quality.IsRemux(name) bool` — the two-arm RemuxRegex from `QualityParser.cs:66`. The C# original captures the matched substring into `(?<remux>...)` named groups on BOTH alternation arms; RE2 rejects duplicate named groups, so the Go port elides the names since the only consumer (`RemuxRegex.IsMatch(...)` at `QualityParser.cs:118`) checks match-success only and never reads the captured text. The two arms are preserved verbatim:

- Branch A (prefix-anchored): `(?:[_. ]|\d{4}p-|\bHybrid-)(?:(?:BD|UHD)[-_. ]?)?Remux\b` — separator/`1080p-`/`Hybrid-` lead, optional `BD`/`UHD` qualifier, then `Remux` followed by a word boundary.
- Branch B (suffix-anchored): `(?:(?:BD|UHD)[-_. ]?)?Remux[_. ]\d{4}p` — `Remux` followed by separator + 4-digit-`p` resolution.

The anchored shape is what rejects false-positive release-group tokens like `[TMS-Remux]` and `[RandomRemux]` — the Remux substring is there but neither arm's anchoring conditions are met. Both false-positive shapes are pinned in the test table; they're real fixture rows from `should_parse_*` tests where the C# regex deliberately classifies the release as non-remux.

3 tests total: ParseCodec table (~15 cases drawn from should_parse_sdtv / should_parse_hdtv720p / should_parse_webdl720p / should_parse_webdl1080p fixture rows + Hi10P brackets edge case) + alternation-order pin (XvidHD vs Xvid leftmost-match); IsRemux table (~17 cases drawn from should_parse_bluray1080p_remux_quality + should_parse_bluray2160p_remux_quality + the two false-positive release-group rows + plain non-remux negatives + branch-B suffix variants). Lint clean; full suite green on both engines under `-race -p 1`.

What's deferred from QualityParser: `SourceRegex` (the big one — 9-branch alternation with `RegexOptions.IgnorePatternWhitespace` and `(?-i:WEB)` inline flag negation), `RawHDRegex`, `OtherSourceRegex`, `AnimeBlurayRegex`, `AnimeWebDlRegex`, `MPEG2Regex`, `HighDefPdtvRegex`, `QualityFinder.FindBySourceAndResolution`, and the per-source decision matrix at `ParseQualityName` itself. ParseSource is the next slice; everything else either ports cleanly alongside it or feeds into the final ParseQualityName commit.

#### 2.7 — ParseSource ✅ shipped (2026-05-03)

The big QualityParser regex slice. `quality.ParseSource(name) SourceTag` ports the 11-branch SourceRegex from `QualityParser.cs:17-30` plus the LastOrDefault selection semantic from the consumer at `:114-115`. Returns one of 12 SourceTag values (Unknown / Bluray / WebDL / WebRip / HDTV / BDRip / BRRip / DVD / DSR / PDTV / SDTV / TVRip).

`SourceTag` is a parser-side classification distinct from the persisted `QualitySource` enum: multiple SourceTag values map to the same QualitySource (BDRip / BRRip / Bluray → QualitySource.Bluray; DSR / PDTV / SDTV / TVRip → QualitySource.Television). The decision matrix at `ParseQualityName` branches on the parser-side tag because each tag has different resolution-fallback rules.

Three RE2 reformulations vs the C# literal documented inline in `parse_source.go`:

1. `RegexOptions.IgnorePatternWhitespace` (REGEX-Q6) — Go's RE2 has no equivalent inline flag. The Go literal is written as a single line with all formatting whitespace removed; whitespace inside character classes is preserved verbatim because the C# `x` flag only ignores whitespace OUTSIDE character classes. One-time conversion; no behavioural change.

2. `BD(?!$)` — RE2 has no negative lookahead. The bare `BD` is pulled into its own named group `blurayBD` so the post-match filter in ParseSource can reject matches where this group's captured text ends at the end of the input string. Functionally equivalent to the C# lookahead because the surrounding regex's trailing `(?:\b|$|[ .])` would otherwise admit the BD-at-end match.

3. `(?:AMZN|NF|DP)[. -]WEB[. -](?!Rip)` — RE2 has no negative lookahead. The AMZN/NF/DP arm is split into its own named group `webdlamzn` so the post-match filter can reject matches where the next 3 bytes after the captured group spell `Rip` (case-insensitive). Both `webdl` and `webdlamzn` map to SourceTagWebDL.

`(?-i:WEB)` is preserved verbatim — Go's RE2 supports inline flag scoping and negation (REGEX-Q7 verified by hand: `(?i)foo(?-i:WEB)$` matches `fooWEB` / `FOOWEB` but not `fooweb`). This keeps the case-sensitive WEB$ branch that distinguishes `Series.1080p.WEB` (matches → WebDL) from `Series.1080p.web` (no match → Unknown).

LastOrDefault semantic preserved: ParseSource walks ALL matches via `FindAllStringSubmatchIndex`, applies the two post-match lookaround filters, and returns the SourceTag of the LAST surviving match. Mirrors the C# `sourceMatches.OfType<Match>().LastOrDefault()` so a release name with multiple source tokens (e.g. `BluRay.x264.HDTV`) resolves to the rightmost hit.

3 tests covering: ParseSource table (~50 cases — every named group exercised plus the two RE2 lookaround filter cases plus underscore-form pre-normalise + multi-source last-wins + empty/no-source negatives), `(?-i:WEB)` case-sensitive flag pin (4 cases), and a fixture-spot-check against 17 verbatim QualityParserFixture rows pulled from should_parse_sdtv / should_parse_dvd / should_parse_webdl / should_parse_webrip / should_parse_bluray fixture methods. Lint clean; full suite green on both engines under `-race -p 1`.

C# behavioural quirks preserved:

- `WEB.Rip` (period-separated) does NOT match the WebRip group — the C# regex only matches `WebRip` / `Web-Rip` / `WEBMux` literals, not period-separated. Consequence: `AMZN.WEB.Rip-Grp` returns Unknown (AMZN/NF/DP-WEB arm filtered out by `(?!Rip)`, no other arm catches the `WEB.Rip` substring). Pinned by test.
- `Web-Rip` arm is theoretically reachable but the resolution-WEB-arm `(?:720|1080|2160)p[-. ]WEB[-. ]` would consume `720p.Web-` first when both appear in the same name, leaving only `Rip.x264` for subsequent matching (which doesn't match anything). Pinned by test comment.
- The `xvidvd` token in the dvd group is a real release-name fragment from `the.Series.1x13.circles.ws.xvidvd-tns` (a fixture row); preserved verbatim as a literal string in the alternation.

What's deferred from QualityParser: `RawHDRegex`, `OtherSourceRegex`, `AnimeBlurayRegex` (uses lookbehind/lookahead — needs separate RE2 rewrite), `AnimeWebDlRegex`, `MPEG2Regex`, `HighDefPdtvRegex`, `QualityFinder.FindBySourceAndResolution`, and the per-source decision matrix at `ParseQualityName` itself. The remaining regexes are mostly small RE2-clean ports plus AnimeBlurayRegex which needs a lookbehind/lookahead rewrite. ParseQualityName lands as the final QualityParser commit once all the input regexes are ported.

#### 2.8 — Misc QualityParser predicates ✅ shipped (2026-05-03)

Final pre-`ParseQualityName` slice. Six small support regexes ported as predicate helpers in `internal/quality/parse_misc.go`. With this commit every input regex `ParseQualityName` consumes is now available — the next QualityParser commit is `ParseQualityName` itself wiring them into the per-source decision matrix.

- `quality.IsRawHD(name) bool` — `\b(?:RawHD|Raw[-_. ]HD)\b`, case-insensitive. RE2-clean. Drives the early-exit at `QualityParser.cs:105` that classifies any RawHD-tagged release as `Quality.RAWHD` regardless of resolution.
- `quality.IsMPEG2(name) bool` — `\b(?:MPEG[-_. ]?2)\b`, case-SENSITIVE per the C# regex declaration (no IgnoreCase flag). RE2-clean. Used at `:231` to flip HDTV+MPEG2 to RAWHD.
- `quality.IsHighDefPdtv(name) bool` — `hr[-_. ]ws`, case-insensitive, NO anchors (substring match). RE2-clean. Used at `:308` to flip PDTV/SDTV/DSR/TVRip to HDTV720p when the HR-WS token is present.
- `quality.IsAnimeWebDL(name) bool` — `\[WEB\]|[\[(]WEB[ .]`, case-insensitive. RE2-clean. Used at `:392` to enter the anime-WebDL branch of ParseQualityName.
- `quality.IsAnimeBluray(name) bool` — the only RE2-rewrite case in this slice. The C# regex `bd(?:720|1080|2160)|(?<=[-_. (\[])bd(?=[-_. )\]])` uses both negative lookbehind AND negative lookahead in arm 2 (zero-width separator assertions on each side of `bd`). RE2 supports neither. The Go port splits into two compiled regexes: arm 1 (`bd(?:720|1080|2160)`) is RE2-clean as written; arm 2 is rewritten as `[-_. (\[]bd[-_. )\]]` — folding the surrounding chars INTO the match. Functionally equivalent for IsMatch on real release names because the C# lookarounds are zero-width on the same character classes; both rewrites pin the asymmetric `(`/`)` and `[`/`]` open-vs-close pairing that matches anime release-naming conventions like `[BD]` and `(BD)`. IsAnimeBluray short-circuits arm 1 first.
- `quality.ClassifyOtherSource(name) SourceTag` — `(?P<hdtv>HD[-_. ]TV)|(?P<sdtv>SD[-_. ]TV)`, case-insensitive. RE2-clean. Returns `SourceTagHDTV` / `SourceTagSDTV` / `SourceTagUnknown`. Mirrors the C# `OtherSourceMatch` private helper at `:653-674` but returns a SourceTag instead of a Quality so the resolution-mapping decision lives in (still-unported) ParseQualityName rather than baked into the primitive.

6 tests / ~70 cases drawn from QualityParserFixture rows where each predicate's classification is the discriminating factor: HR-WS PDTV (lines 149-150), MPEG2-TrollHD (lines 386-393), HorribleSubs `[Web]` (96, 212-213, 255, 286), LostYears/Netaro `(WEB ` (256, 260), FFF/coldhell `[BD]` and `[BD720p]/[BD1080p]` (311-312, 332-333), HD.TV/SD.TV final-fallback (461-462). Plus separator-class permutations (`-`, `_`, `.`, ` `), case-sensitivity pins (MPEG2 case-sensitive; everything else case-insensitive), and the IsAnimeBluray bare-`bd` separator-anchor edge cases. Lint clean; full suite green on both engines under `-race -p 1`.

C# behavioural quirks preserved: the asymmetric paren/bracket pairing in IsAnimeBluray arm 2 (`(`/`)` and `[`/`]` only — never `(`/`]` or `[`/`)`), and the case-SENSITIVITY of MPEG2Regex (declared without IgnoreCase in the C# tree even though every other QualityParser regex IS case-insensitive — preserved verbatim because lowercase `mpeg2` does not appear in real release names per the fixture).

#### 2.9 — ParseQuality + QualityFinder + MediaFileExtensions ✅ shipped (2026-05-03)

QualityParser slice complete. Three new modules wired together to produce the full `quality.ParseQuality(name) Model` end-to-end:

- `internal/quality/finder.go` — `FindBySourceAndResolution(source, resolution) Quality`. Mirrors `QualityFinder.FindBySourceAndResolution` at `src/NzbDrone.Core/Qualities/QualityFinder.cs:11-52`. Three-step decision: exact-match, sub-720 source-specific fallback (Television→SDTV, Web→WEBDL480p, WebRip→WEBRip480p), nearest-source-at-resolution scan. The C# logger warning on the fallback path is omitted because logging infrastructure isn't wired through in this package yet — caller-side logging will be added when the service layer lands.

- `internal/quality/extensions.go` — `GetQualityForExtension(ext) Quality` plus the 43-entry `extensionQualities` map. Mirrors `MediaFileExtensions._fileExtensions` + `GetQualityForExtension` at `src/NzbDrone.Core/MediaFiles/MediaFileExtensions.cs:11-84`. **Naming exception**: the C# tree puts this in `NzbDrone.Core.MediaFiles`; the Go port colocates here because `quality.ParseQuality` is the only consumer and a separate `internal/mediafiles` package would create an import cycle (mediafiles would import quality for the Quality type; quality.ParseQuality needs mediafiles for the lookup). When the broader MediaFiles namespace lands in a later phase, this map can be moved out and re-exported via a small forwarding package. Decision noted in the file's package comment.

- `internal/quality/parse.go` — `ParseQuality(name) Model` + `ParseQualityName(name) Model`. Mirrors `QualityParser.ParseQuality` + `ParseQualityName` at `QualityParser.cs:68-598`. The control flow follows the C# source line-for-line (each labelled section cites the source line ranges) so a future sync against the C# tree is direct. The decision matrix dispatches on `SourceTag` (the parser-side classification from Phase 2.7) into per-source sub-trees: Bluray decision tree, WebDL/WebRip/HDTV resolution-mapped, BDRip/BRRip → Bluray-by-resolution, DVD passthrough, DSR/PDTV/SDTV/TVRip with `containsCI` resolution-token fallback. After the source-driven branches: source-less remux fallback (resolution determines Bluray sub-quality), anime Bluray + anime WebDL fallbacks, resolution-only fallback (with extension-driven source guess), bare x264 → SDTV, 848x480/1280x720/1920x1080 token fallbacks, bluray720p/1080p/2160p concatenated-token fallback, final HD-TV/SD-TV via OtherSourceRegex.

Two helper utilities live alongside:

- `containsCI(s, substr) bool` — case-insensitive substring check mirroring C# `ContainsIgnoreCase`. Inlined byte-loop avoids two `strings.ToLower` allocations per call (called many times across the decision matrix).
- `getPathExtension(path)` — substring-from-last-dot, mirroring `string.GetPathExtension()` at `src/NzbDrone.Common/Extensions/PathExtensions.cs:74-83`. NOT equivalent to Go's `filepath.Ext` because the Sonarr helper operates on the full string regardless of `\`/`/` separators.
- `containsInvalidPathChars(s) bool` — mirrors `string.ContainsInvalidPathChars()` (delegates to .NET `Path.GetInvalidPathChars`'s cross-platform set: control chars 0x00–0x1F + `|`). Used in ParseQuality + the resolution-only fallback to skip the extension-lookup branch when `Path.GetExtension` would refuse the input — preserves the C# try/catch semantic without actually throwing.

Tests: ~70 cases across 6 test functions — `TestParseQuality_FixtureRows` (~50 cases drawn 3-5 per fixture method from QualityParserFixture rows), `TestParseQuality_DetectionSources` (~13 cases from the `should_parse_*_from_*` methods), `TestParseQuality_RepackVersion`, `TestParseQuality_AnimeVersion`, `TestParseQuality_EmptyInput`, `TestParseQuality_SelfQualityEnumName` (16 cases — `My series S01E01 [<Quality.Name>]` for each canonical Quality, exercising the resolution-only fallback paths plus the Bluray720p/1080p/2160p concatenated-token fallbacks). Plus `TestFindBySourceAndResolution` (~14 cases pinning the three-step decision) and `TestGetQualityForExtension` (~18 cases sampling each Quality bucket + case-insensitive lookup + negatives).

All tests passed first run (the line-for-line port from C# was reliable). Lint clean; full suite green on both engines under `-race -p 1`.
