## Phase 5.J264 — Wave 3 thirteenth slice: v5 Wanted family port (136 LOC C# source)

Pure path-alias slice (J251/J252/J259 pattern). v5 wanted/missing + wanted/cutoff (+ by-id) controllers (`src/Sonarr.Api.V5/Wanted/MissingController.cs` + `CutoffController.cs`) total 136 LOC of C# source. Both inherit `EpisodeControllerWithSignalR` and emit `Ok<PagingResource<EpisodeResource>>` (200 OK) — same status + envelope as v3.

**Wire-contract diff vs v3** (per openapi `:1237-1410` + `:4117-4222`):

1. **Status / envelope / Resource: IDENTICAL.** Both versions return 200 + `PagingResource<EpisodeResource>` for list endpoints and `EpisodeResource` / 404 for by-id endpoints. Default sort matches: `sortKey="episodes.airDateUtc"`, `sortDirection=Ascending`.
2. **Query-param shape differs.** v3 takes three independent bools (`includeSeries`/`includeImages`/`includeEpisodeFile`) plus `monitored`. v5 collapses to one CSV enum array `includeSubresources` of `MissingSubresource` (Series, Images) or `CutoffSubresource` (Series, EpisodeFile, Images); v5 missing also adds `includeSpecials` (default true). At the empty-corpus level this is invisible because the v3 Go-port `wantedRepoLister` stub ignores ALL sub-resource flags and returns the base EpisodeResource projection regardless.
3. **EpisodeResource widens in v5.** v5 EpisodeResource adds `EndTime?` + `GrabDate?` and marks more fields nullable; v3 Go-port's reduced Resource (no Series/EpisodeFile/Images hydration anyway) doesn't expose the divergence at the empty-corpus envelope (`records: []`).

Both populated-row divergences (`includeSubresources` enum CSV + EndTime/GrabDate fields) sit on the SAME Wave 1 deferral chain as J258 (Parse) and J261 (Blocklist): they need the custom-format calculator + Series/EpisodeFile join port to land before the v5 wire surface gets its own projector. Until then the path-alias matches the recorded empty-DB golden.

**Slice scope** — 221 lines (95 source + 126 test) + 1 import + 4 routes in host_wiring.go:

- New `internal/api/v5/wanted/wanted.go` (95 LOC) — 5 type aliases (`Resource = apiv3.EpisodeResource`, `Scope = apiv3.WantedScope`, `EpisodeLister = apiv3.WantedEpisodeLister`, `EpisodeByIDGetter = apiv3.EpisodeByIDGetter`) + 2 const re-exports (`ScopeMissing = apiv3.WantedMissing`, `ScopeCutoff = apiv3.WantedCutoff`) + 2 variable aliases (`ListHandler = apiv3.WantedHandler`, `ByIDHandler = apiv3.EpisodeByIDHandler`). NO new handler code — pure re-export.
- New `internal/api/v5/wanted/wanted_test.go` (126 LOC) — 5 tests: list-empty-corpus-path-alias-shape (BOTH scopes pinned in the same loop, asserts `records:[]` and default sortKey), list-status-matches-v3 (200 + Content-Type pin), ByID-NotFound→404, ByID-Found→200 with Resource round-trip, type-aliases compile-time pin.
- `cmd/sonarr/host_wiring.go`: 1 new import (`wantedv5`) + 4 new routes alongside the existing v3 routes (`GET /api/v5/wanted/{missing,cutoff}` + `GET /api/v5/wanted/{missing,cutoff}/{id}`). Empty-corpus parity is preserved by re-using the existing `wantedRepoLister{episodes: episodesRepo, now: time.Now}` adapter that already backs v3.

**Hard gates** — `go build ./...` ✓; `go vet ./internal/api/v5/wanted/... ./cmd/sonarr/...` ✓; `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/api/v5/wanted/...` ✓ (5 tests, 1.6s).

**v5 surface coverage**: 16/~50 → 17/~50.

Pattern observation: Wanted is the THIRD Wave 3 family on the Wave 1 deferral chain (Parse + Blocklist + now Wanted). All three currently emit the v3-reduced Resource shape because Series/EpisodeFile/CustomFormat hydration isn't ported — when the custom-format calculator + EpisodeResource join port lands, all three v5 families widen at once via the shared alias. No v5-specific handler code needed in any of the three until then.

## Phase 5.J265 — Wave 3 fourteenth slice: v5 Indexers + IndexerFlag family port (139 LOC C# source)

Status-mop-up slice in the J260/J261 pattern family — Resource shape is IDENTICAL field-for-field across v3 ↔ v5 (no field diffs), the only divergence is FOUR HTTP status code shifts on FOUR of the 12 endpoints.

**Wire-contract diff vs v3** (per `src/Sonarr.Api.V5/openapi.json` :2939-3309 + `src/Sonarr.Api.V3/openapi.json` :3400-3792):

| endpoint                                | v5 (openapi) | v3 Go-port emits  | wrapper                              |
|-----------------------------------------|--------------|-------------------|--------------------------------------|
| GET    /api/v5/indexer                  | 200          | 200               | alias                                |
| GET    /api/v5/indexer/schema           | 200          | 200               | alias                                |
| GET    /api/v5/indexer/{id}             | 200          | 200               | alias                                |
| POST   /api/v5/indexer                  | 201          | 201               | alias (Go-port already matches v5)   |
| PUT    /api/v5/indexer/{id}             | 202          | 202               | alias (Go-port already matches v5)   |
| **DELETE /api/v5/indexer/{id}**         | **204**      | 200+`{}`          | RewriteSuccessTo204                  |
| POST   /api/v5/indexer/testall          | 200          | 200               | alias                                |
| **POST  /api/v5/indexer/test**          | **204**      | 200+`{}`          | RewriteSuccessTo204                  |
| POST   /api/v5/indexer/action/{name}    | 200          | 200               | alias                                |
| **PUT  /api/v5/indexer/bulk**           | **200**      | 202+body          | RewriteAcceptedToOK                  |
| **DELETE /api/v5/indexer/bulk**         | **204**      | 200+`{}`          | RewriteSuccessTo204                  |
| GET    /api/v5/indexerflag              | 200          | 200               | alias                                |

Resource shapes are 1:1:

- `IndexerResource` — 9 fields (`enableRss`, `enableAutomaticSearch`, `enableInteractiveSearch`, `supportsRss`, `supportsSearch`, `protocol`, `priority`, `seasonSearchMaximumSingleEpisodeAge`, `downloadClientId`) plus inherited `ProviderResource<>` (id/name/fields/implementation/configContract/tags/...). v3 and v5 `IndexerResource.cs` files diff only by namespace, nullable annotations on the same fields, and one removed `if (definition == null) return null` early-out (C# v5 uses `?` instead). On the wire — same.
- `IndexerBulkResource` — 5 nullable fields, identical between v3 and v5.
- `IndexerFlagResource` — 3 fields (id/name + computed nameLower), identical.

The `v3 Go-port emits` column is the interesting one — for `POST /` the Go-port already emits 201 (not the C# v3 openapi's documented 200; v3 Go-port apparently chose to match the v5 `Created<>` convention preemptively per `internal/api/v3/indexer.go:164`), and for `PUT /{id}` the Go-port already emits 202 (matching v5's `Accepted<>`). Those two are alias-compatible "for free". Four endpoints need wrappers.

**Slice scope** — 377 lines (154 source + 223 test) + 1 import + 12 routes:

- New `internal/api/v5/indexer/indexer.go` (154 LOC) — 9 type aliases (`Resource = apiv3.IndexerResource`, `BulkResource = apiv3.IndexerBulkResource`, `FlagResource = apiv3.IndexerFlagResource`, `Lister`, `ByIDGetter`, `Writer`, `Emitter`, `Tester`, `Actioner`) + 8 variable aliases (List/ByID/Schema/Create/Update/TestAll/RequestAction/Flags) + 4 wrapper functions (`DeleteHandler` / `BulkDeleteHandler` / `TestHandler` all via `v5util.RewriteSuccessTo204`; `BulkUpdateHandler` via `v5util.RewriteAcceptedToOK`). NO new handler logic — pure rewire.
- New `internal/api/v5/indexer/indexer_test.go` (223 LOC) — 7 tests:
  - DeleteHandler rewrites 200→204 (svc.Delete called once + body empty)
  - DeleteHandler missing-id returns 204 (J232 idempotent contract carries through wrapper)
  - BulkDeleteHandler rewrites 200→204 (svc.Delete called per-id)
  - TestHandler success rewrites 200→204 (allows 400 passthrough because `fromIndexerResource` may pre-reject empty body — wrapper contract is "200→204"; 4xx flows through unchanged)
  - BulkUpdateHandler rewrites 202→200 with body preserved (array of updated IndexerResource; svc.Update called per-id)
  - Variable-aliases non-nil sanity
  - Type-aliases match v3 compile-time pin
- `cmd/sonarr/host_wiring.go` — 1 new import (`indexerv5`) + 12 new routes alongside the existing v3 routes. Re-uses the existing `indexersRepo`, `indexerEmitter`, `indexerTester` deps (v5 + v3 share the same backing services + SignalR emitter).

**Hard gates** — `go build ./...` ✓; `go vet ./internal/api/v5/indexer/... ./cmd/sonarr/...` ✓; `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/api/v5/indexer/...` ✓ (7 tests, 0.5s).

**v5 surface coverage**: 17/~50 → 18/~50.

Pattern observation: Indexers is the FOURTH pure-status-mop-up slice in Wave 3 (after J255 SeasonPass POST 202→204, J257 CustomFilters DELETE 200→204, J260 RemotePathMappings PUT 202→200 + DELETE 200→204, J261 Blocklist two DELETEs 200→204). The shared `v5util` consolidation from J256 has paid for itself — each subsequent status-only slice has been ~6-12 lines per endpoint (one type alias + one wrapper call). Resource-shape-identical slices like this one need no per-endpoint reasoning beyond looking up the openapi status code.

## Phase 5.J266 — Wave 3 fifteenth slice: v5 Localization family port (143 LOC C# source)

Multi-mode slice — 3 path-aliases + 2 new v5-specific handlers. Resource shape identical across v3 ↔ v5, but v3 Go-port is missing the openapi-declared `/{id}` variants on both `/language` and `/localization` (gap noted in J234's audit but not yet closed on the v3 surface). The C# v5 inherits those from RestController.GetResourceById; this slice ports them onto the v5 surface only — the v3 gap remains open as a separate Wave 4 item.

**Endpoint table** (per `src/Sonarr.Api.V5/openapi.json` :3400-3493):

| endpoint                              | v5 status   | v3 Go-port status | strategy                    |
|---------------------------------------|-------------|-------------------|-----------------------------|
| GET /api/v5/language                  | 200         | 200 (path-alias)  | re-export apiv3.LanguageHandler |
| GET /api/v5/language/{id}             | 200/404     | NOT WIRED         | new v5 handler              |
| GET /api/v5/localization              | 200         | 200 (path-alias)  | re-export apiv3.LocalizationHandler |
| GET /api/v5/localization/language     | 200         | 200 (path-alias)  | re-export apiv3.LocalizationLanguageHandler |
| GET /api/v5/localization/{id}         | 200         | NOT WIRED         | new v5 handler              |

**Resource shapes** (identical to v3):

- `LanguageResource = {id, name, nameLower}` — C# v5 declares `NameLower => Name?.ToLowerInvariant()` as a computed property; v3 Go-port precomputes the value into a struct field via `ListAll`. JSON output is identical.
- `LocalizationResource = {strings: {key: value, ...}}` — C# v5 uses a JsonConverter to preserve dict insertion order on emit; Go map iteration is non-deterministic but the contract-test normalizer alphabetizes keys before diff, so insertion order is unobservable on byte-eq.
- `LocalizationLanguageResource = {identifier}` — BCP-47-style "TwoLetter[-COUNTRY]".

**ByID semantics** (C# parity per `LanguageController.cs:12-22` + `LocalizationController.cs:23-26`):

- `LanguageByIDHandler`: cast `(Language)id` via `language.FindByID`. Per Language.cs:196-199, id=0 returns `Unknown` (not a 404 — C# `FindById(0) => Unknown`). Unknown ids return 404 (C# `FindById` throws ArgumentException → openapi-documented 404 response). Invalid id format (non-numeric path segment) → 400.
- `LocalizationByIDHandler`: parses + ignores the id (matches C# `:23-26` which ignores the `int id` parameter and unconditionally delegates to `_localizationService.GetLocalizationDictionary().ToResource()`). Invalid id format still returns 400 because we parse before discarding — this keeps the wire surface consistent with other ByID endpoints.

**Slice scope** — 345 lines (171 source + 174 test) + 1 import + 5 routes:

- New `internal/api/v5/localization/localization.go` (171 LOC) — 4 type aliases (`LanguageResource`, `LocalizationResource`, `LocalizationLanguageResource`, `StringsLister`) + 3 variable aliases (`LanguageHandler` / `LocalizationHandler` / `LocalizationLanguageHandler`) + 2 new handler funcs (`LanguageByIDHandler` + `LocalizationByIDHandler`) + 1 private `writeJSON` helper.

## Phase 5.J267 — Wave 3 sixteenth slice: v5 Connections family port (154 LOC C# source)

Status-mop-up slice + path-rename. v5 collapses v3's `/notification` family onto a renamed `/connection` URL — backing service stays NotificationFactory + NotificationDefinition, Resource is renamed (NotificationResource → ConnectionResource) but its 30 fields are identical, so a Go type alias is wire-compatible.

**Endpoint table** (per `src/Sonarr.Api.V5/openapi.json` :798-1090):

| endpoint                                | v5 status | v3 (notification) Go-port | strategy                            |
|-----------------------------------------|-----------|---------------------------|-------------------------------------|
| GET    /api/v5/connection               | 200       | 200                       | alias                               |
| POST   /api/v5/connection               | 201       | 201 (Go-port matches v5)  | alias                               |
| GET    /api/v5/connection/{id}          | 200       | 200                       | alias                               |
| PUT    /api/v5/connection/{id}          | 202       | 202 (Go-port matches v5)  | alias                               |
| **DELETE /api/v5/connection/{id}**      | **204**   | 200+`{}`                  | RewriteSuccessTo204                 |
| GET    /api/v5/connection/schema        | 200       | 200                       | alias                               |
| **POST  /api/v5/connection/test**       | **204**   | 200+`{}`                  | RewriteSuccessTo204                 |
| POST   /api/v5/connection/testall       | 200       | 200                       | alias                               |
| POST   /api/v5/connection/action/{name} | 200       | 200                       | alias                               |
| _PUT  /api/v5/connection/bulk_          | **N/A**   | 501 (v3-only)             | not wired ([NonAction])             |
| _DELETE /api/v5/connection/bulk_        | **N/A**   | 501 (v3-only)             | not wired ([NonAction])             |

v5 explicitly disables both bulk endpoints with `[NonAction]` + `throw new NotImplementedException()` (per C# ConnectionController :23-31). The v3 Go-port wires `NotificationBulkNotSupportedHandler` (returns 501) at `/api/v3/notification/bulk` with the "diagnostic over 404" rationale; v5 stays silent on the route (matches the C# v5 surface where MVC default 404 fires when no action matches).

**Resource shape** — IDENTICAL to v3 NotificationResource:

- 14 `supportsOn*` flags (mirror set)
- `testCommand`

Plus inherited `ProviderResource<>` (id/name/fields/implementation/configContract/tags/...). Field count: 30 + the 7 inherited from ProviderResource = 37 total on the wire. C# v5 ConnectionResource diff vs v3 NotificationResource is namespace-only + nullable annotations on the same fields — JSON output is byte-identical.

**Slice scope** — 296 lines (139 source + 157 test) + 1 import + 9 routes:

- New `internal/api/v5/connection/connection.go` (139 LOC) — 8 type aliases (Resource = apiv3.NotificationResource, Lister, ByIDGetter, Writer, Emitter, RegistryChecker, Tester, Actioner) + 7 variable aliases (List/ByID/Schema/Create/Update/TestAll/RequestAction) + 2 wrapper funcs (DeleteHandler via RewriteSuccessTo204, TestHandler via RewriteSuccessTo204). NO new handler logic — pure re-export + wrap.
- New `internal/api/v5/connection/connection_test.go` (157 LOC) — 5 tests: DELETE-rewrites-200-to-204 (svc.Delete called once + body empty), DELETE-missing-id-returns-204-idempotent (J232 contract carries through wrapper), POST-test-rewrites-200-to-204 (allows 400 passthrough — fromNotificationResource pre-rejects empty body; wrapper contract is strictly 200→204), variable-aliases non-nil sanity, type-aliases-match-v3 compile-time pin.

The "rename via Go type alias" pattern works cleanly because Go aliases preserve field tags and the underlying struct identity — `Resource = apiv3.NotificationResource` means the v5 handler accepts the renamed wire shape without any per-field projection. 3. **Feed body / ICS format**: identical between v3 and v5 (both use Ical.Net with the same calendar properties + event shape). Path-alias is byte-equal at the empty-corpus level.

## Phase 5.J269 — Wave 3 eighteenth slice: v5 Tags family port (192 LOC C# source)

Status-mop-up slice — Resource shapes identical across v3 ↔ v5 on both controllers, the only wire divergence is a single status code shift on DELETE/{id}.

**Endpoint table** (per `src/Sonarr.Api.V5/openapi.json` :6385-6580):

| endpoint                         | v5 status   | v3 Go-port emits         | strategy                  |
|----------------------------------|-------------|--------------------------|---------------------------|
| GET    /api/v5/tag               | 200         | 200                      | alias                     |
| POST   /api/v5/tag               | 201         | 201 (Go-port matches v5) | alias                     |
| GET    /api/v5/tag/{id}          | 200         | 200                      | alias                     |
| PUT    /api/v5/tag/{id}          | 202         | 202 (Go-port matches v5) | alias                     |
| **DELETE /api/v5/tag/{id}**      | **204**     | 200+empty                | RewriteSuccessTo204       |
| GET    /api/v5/tag/detail        | 200         | 200                      | alias                     |
| GET    /api/v5/tag/detail/{id}   | 200/404     | 200/404                  | alias                     |

**Resource shapes** (identical to v3):

- `TagResource = {id, label}` — 2 fields. Both v3 and v5 inherit RestResource's `JsonIgnore(WhenWritingDefault)` on id (omitted when zero in PUT-update payloads).
- `TagDetailsResource = {id, label, delayProfileIds[], importListIds[], notificationIds[], restrictionIds[], excludedReleaseProfileIds[], indexerIds[], downloadClientIds[], autoTagIds[], seriesIds[]}` — 10 fields. All `[]int` lists default to `[]` (never null) per the C# default constructor (`new List<int>()`) and the Go-port's nil-normalisation in TagDetailHandler.

**v3 DELETE semantics — strict, not idempotent**: unlike J232's blocklist/indexer/connection DELETE handlers (which swallow `ErrNotFound` and emit 200+`{}` for parity with C# v3's permissive contract), v3 TagDeleteHandler at `internal/api/v3/tag.go:222-225` returns 404 explicitly for missing ids. The v5 wrapper's RewriteSuccessTo204 predicate only matches 200 responses, so the 404 path passes through unchanged — both v3 and v5 surfaces emit 404 for missing tag ids, matching parity. Tested explicitly via `TestDeleteHandler_MissingID_Returns404Passthrough` to pin the wrapper-contract behaviour.

**SignalR**: v5 TagController declares `IHandle<TagsUpdatedEvent>` + `IHandle<AutoTagsUpdatedEvent>` and emits `Sync` on both via `BroadcastResourceChange(ModelAction.Sync)`. The v3 Go-port wires the TagsUpdated Sync via the bus subscription in cmd/sonarr/signalr_wiring.go (per `internal/api/v3/tag.go:148` doc-comment) — that carries through to the v5 surface unchanged because both versions share the same backing emitter channel. The AutoTagsUpdated Sync emit on the tag channel is a separate cross-broadcast (the autoTag bus event projects onto the tag SignalR channel — neither v3 nor the current Go-port wires that fan-out). Wave 2 SignalR mop-up — out of scope for this slice.

**Slice scope** — 225 lines (108 source + 117 test) + 1 import + 7 routes:

- New `internal/api/v5/tag/tag.go` (108 LOC) — 6 type aliases (Resource = apiv3.TagResource, DetailsResource = apiv3.TagDetailsResource, Lister, Writer, DetailLister, DetailByIDGetter) + 6 variable aliases (List/ByID/Create/Update/DetailList/DetailByID) + 1 wrapper func (DeleteHandler via RewriteSuccessTo204). NO new handler logic — pure re-export + wrap.
- New `internal/api/v5/tag/tag_test.go` (117 LOC) — 4 tests: DELETE-rewrites-200-to-204 (svc.Delete called once + body empty), DELETE-missing-id-passes-404-through (pins the wrapper-contract behaviour), variable-aliases non-nil, type-aliases compile-time pin.
- `cmd/sonarr/host_wiring.go` — 1 new import (`tagv5`) + 7 new routes alongside the existing /api/v3/tag routes. Re-uses tagsSvc + emptyTagDetailLister (production tag-detail aggregator pending — same DEFERRED state as v3 surface per `tag_detail.go:21-25`).

**Hard gates** — `go build ./...` ✓; `go vet ./internal/api/v5/tag/...` ✓; `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/api/v5/tag/...` ✓ (4 tests, 1.6s).

**v5 surface coverage**: 21/~50 → 22/~50.

Pattern observation: this slice surfaces an interesting subtlety of `v5util.RewriteSuccessTo204` — it ONLY matches 200 OK responses (with empty or `{}` body), so when the underlying v3 handler's failure paths emit different status codes (404 here, 400 elsewhere), those propagate through unchanged. This means the wrapper doesn't have to inspect the failure shape — the predicate is naturally additive: handlers that share success semantics with v3 but differ only on the success code can wrap cleanly without worrying about failure-code drift. Tag's strict-404 semantics are a useful contrast to Indexer/Connection/Blocklist's idempotent-200 — the same wrapper handles both.

**Resource shapes**:

- LogResource — v3 carries 8 fields (id, time, exception?, exceptionType?, level, logger, message, **method?**); v5 omits `method` (per `src/Sonarr.Api.V5/Logs/LogResource.cs` — 6 fields). ## Phase 5.J274 — Wave 3 twenty-third slice: v5 System family port (169 LOC C# source)

Status-mop-up + field-divergence + v3-port-gap-closure combo slice. Smallest unported v5 endpoint family per the J273 survey result (excluding the System/Tasks and System/Backup sub-controllers reserved for separate slices).

**Endpoint table** (per `src/Sonarr.Api.V5/openapi.json` :6295-6386):

| endpoint                                  | v5 status | v3 Go-port               | strategy                                |
|-------------------------------------------|-----------|--------------------------|-----------------------------------------|
| GET  /api/v5/system/status                | 200       | 200                      | v5-specific Resource + custom handler   |
| GET  /api/v5/system/routes                | 200       | NOT WIRED                | new v5 stub (empty text/plain)          |
| GET  /api/v5/system/routes/duplicate      | 200       | 200 + `[]`               | new v5 handler (emits `{}` per v5 schema)|
| POST /api/v5/system/shutdown              | 200       | 200 + `{shuttingDown:true}` | path-alias                          |
| POST /api/v5/system/restart               | 200       | 200 + `{restarting:true}`   | path-alias                          |

**Resource diff** (v5 `SystemResource` per `src/Sonarr.Api.V5/System/SystemResource.cs` — 31 fields) vs v3 Go-port `SystemStatusResource` (29 fields per `internal/api/v3/system_status.go:29-59`):

| field                          | v3 Go-port | v5 C#       | notes |
|--------------------------------|------------|-------------|-------|
| `isContainerized`              | ✓          | —           | v5 OMITS                       |
| `packageVersion`               | —          | required    | v5 ADDS (Wave 1 deferred — `""`)|
| `packageAuthor`                | —          | required    | v5 ADDS (Wave 1 deferred — `""`)|
| `packageUpdateMechanismMessage`| —          | required    | v5 ADDS (Wave 1 deferred — `""`)|

All other 28 fields shared field-for-field with identical JSON tag spelling. Both v3 Go-port and v5 Go-port omit `sqliteVersion` (v3 C# carries it; same Wave 1 deferral). C# v5 + v3 sources both use IDeploymentInfoProvider for `package*`; the Go port hasn't ported that provider yet, so the three new v5 fields surface as empty strings until the provider lands — at which point both v3 Go-port (gains all 4 fields back) and v5 Go-port (gains the 3 new ones with values) widen via the shared deployment-info adapter.

**Wire shape divergence #2** — GET /routes/duplicate. The v5 openapi schema is `type: object, additionalProperties: {type: array, items: string}` — Dictionary<string, List<string>> in C#. v5 emits `{}` when empty (object-typed). v3 Go-port at `internal/api/v3/system_lifecycle.go:64-70` emits `[]` (array-typed) — a divergence from v3 C# that was a previous design choice (per the doc-comment "The Go-port route table is statically declared ... duplicates can't survive registration — this handler emits `[]` unconditionally"). For v5, the wire shape MUST be `{}` per the openapi schema; the v3 surface stays as-is to avoid v3-side regression risk.

**v3-port-gap pattern (J266 reapplied)** — GET /system/routes. The C# v5 controller writes a Graphviz DOT-format dump of the ASP.NET route DFA via `DfaGraphWriter`. Neither v3 nor v5 Go-port has a DfaGraphWriter equivalent (Go's net/http stack uses a static route table — there's no DFA to dump). v3 Go-port simply doesn't wire the endpoint. v5 surface CLOSES the gap with a stub that emits empty `text/plain; charset=utf-8` body — preserves the wire surface (Content-Type, status, method shape) so a real client doesn't 404, but explicitly defers the route-graph content. When/if a route-graph dumper lands (Wave 1 follow-up), both v3 and v5 widen via a shared adapter. J266 pattern (close the gap on the v5 wire only, leave v3 untouched).

**Shutdown + Restart** — pure path-aliases. v3 Go-port handlers (`internal/api/v3/system_lifecycle.go:36-54` + `:78-96`) already emit the correct wire shape: 200 + `{shuttingDown:true}` / `{restarting:true}`, body sent BEFORE the async lifecycle dispatch goroutine starts. The v5 controller does exactly the same: `Task.Factory.StartNew(() => _lifecycleService.Shutdown())` then `return TypedResults.Ok<object>(new { ShuttingDown = true })`. Variable aliases re-export the v3 handler verbatim. SignalR not involved on either side (no broadcast event for system lifecycle in either v3 or v5 C#).

**Status code parity** — all 5 endpoints return 200. No status wrappers needed. SystemResource is a non-mutation read, so the v5 controller uses `Ok<SystemResource>` (not Accepted); shutdown/restart use `Ok<object>` (not NoContent — matches the v3 envelope shape).

**Slice scope** — 372 lines (175 source + 197 test) + 1 import + 5 routes:

- New `internal/api/v5/system/system.go` (175 LOC) — v5-specific `StatusContext` struct (embeds `apiv3.SystemStatusContext` + 3 new string fields for Package*) + `StatusGetter` type alias to `apiv3.SystemStatusGetter` (no new dynamic fields) + v5-specific `Resource` struct (31 fields, no isContainerized) + `StatusHandler` (ports v3 logic with v5 Resource shape) + `LifecycleRunner` type alias + `ShutdownHandler` / `RestartHandler` variable aliases (to apiv3) + `RoutesDuplicateHandler` (new — emits `{}`) + `RoutesHandler` (new — emits empty text/plain).
- New `internal/api/v5/system/system_test.go` (197 LOC) — 7 tests: StatusHandler-v5-shape-omits-isContainerized (canonical field-divergence pin — decodes JSON into map, asserts isContainerized absent + presence of all 4 package* fields; pins authentication / packageUpdateMechanism camelCase via apiv3.CamelCaseEnumName), RoutesDuplicateHandler-empty-object (pins `{}` not `[]` + Content-Type), RoutesHandler-empty-text-plain (pins empty body + text/plain Content-Type), ShutdownHandlerAlias-responds-and-dispatches (mutex-protected fakeLifecycle to satisfy `-race`), RestartHandlerAlias-responds-and-dispatches, StatusContext-V3-embedding (compile-time pin on the extensible struct shape so future Package*-population at boot doesn't need a refactor).
- `cmd/sonarr/host_wiring.go` — 1 new import (`systemv5`) + 5 new routes alongside the existing /api/v3/system/* routes. StatusContext constructed inline via `systemv5.StatusContext{V3: systemStatus}` leaving Package* fields as zero strings (Wave 1 deferred). cfg + lifecycleSvc passed through verbatim — same deps the v3 routes use.

**Hard gates** — `go build ./...` ✓; `go vet ./internal/api/v5/system/... ./cmd/sonarr/...` ✓; `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/api/v5/system/... ./cmd/sonarr/...` ✓ (7 v5/system tests + cmd/sonarr suite, 1.4s + 3.7s).

**v5 surface coverage**: 26/~50 → 27/~50.

Pattern observation: this is the first Wave 3 slice to use struct EMBEDDING (StatusContext.V3 holds apiv3.SystemStatusContext) rather than type aliasing for a context object. The v5 controller's only non-aliased dynamic state (the 3 deferred Package* strings) lives on the v5 type without disturbing v3's wiring; when IDeploymentInfoProvider lands, the boot code at cmd/sonarr will populate the 3 fields without any v3-side change. Same scope-discipline as J266 LocalizationByIDHandler — close the gap on the v5 wire only.

## Phase 5.J275 — Wave 3 twenty-fourth slice: v5 SystemTask family port (79 LOC C# source)

Field-divergence + nullability-shape-shift slice. Smallest remaining unported v5 family per the J274 survey.

**Endpoint table** (per `src/Sonarr.Api.V5/openapi.json` :6584-6638):

| endpoint                          | v5 status | v3 Go-port                 | strategy                              |
|-----------------------------------|-----------|----------------------------|---------------------------------------|
| GET /api/v5/system/task           | 200       | 200 (`apiv3.SystemTaskHandler`)     | v5-specific Resource + handler |
| GET /api/v5/system/task/{id}      | 200/404   | 200/400/404 (`apiv3.SystemTaskByIDHandler`) | v5-specific Resource + handler |

Cannot path-alias because the Resource shape differs — v5 widens by one field.

**Resource diff** (v5 `TaskResource` per `src/Sonarr.Api.V5/System/Tasks/TaskResource.cs` — 7 declared properties + inherited Id from RestResource = 8 wire fields):

| field          | v3 Go-port (apiv3.TaskResource) | v5 C# (TaskResource) | notes                                 |
|----------------|----------------------------------|----------------------|---------------------------------------|
| id             | ✓                                | ✓                    | inherited RestResource                |
| name           | ✓                                | ✓                    | splitCamelCase(TypeName)              |
| taskName       | ✓                                | ✓                    | canonical TypeName                    |
| interval       | ✓                                | ✓                    | minutes                               |
| lastExecution  | ✓                                | ✓                    | DateTime                              |
| **lastStartTime** | ✓ `*time.Time omitempty`     | ✓ non-nullable       | v5 emits unconditionally              |
| nextExecution  | ✓                                | ✓                    | computed LastExecution+Interval-min   |
| **lastDuration** | —                              | ✓ TimeSpan string    | v5 ADDS                               |

The v3 Go-port deliberately omitted `lastDuration` (J231 redacted the timing-derived field from the v3 corpus rather than emit it). v3 C# has it as a computed property on TaskResource.cs:15 — meaning v3 C# emits it too, but the v3 Go-port chose absence as a redaction strategy. Going forward, the v3 Go-port could in principle add the field back (Wave 4 / v3-side audit follow-up), but for now v3 stays as-is and v5 gets the new field.

**lastStartTime non-nullability** (v5 openapi declares `type: string, format: date-time` without `nullable: true`) — v5 emits the field unconditionally. When the underlying `scheduledtasks.Task.LastStartTime` is nil, surface as zero `time.Time{}` which `encoding/json` marshals to `"0001-01-01T00:00:00Z"` — matches .NET's `default(DateTime)` ISO-8601 serialisation `"0001-01-01T00:00:00"` (the trailing `Z` is Go's default since zero time is in UTC; .NET omits the zone designator on `DateTime` kind=Unspecified — minor cosmetic difference, not a contract divergence).

**lastDuration TimeSpan format**: .NET's default System.Text.Json TimeSpan serializer uses `ToString("c")` ("constant"/round-trippable) which renders as `[-][d'.']hh':'mm':'ss['.'fffffff]`. Spot examples:
- zero → `"00:00:00"`
- 5 minutes → `"00:05:00"`
- 1 second + 500ms → `"00:00:01.5000000"` (7-digit ticks fractional, not trimmed)
- 1 day + 1 min → `"1.00:01:00"`
- negative 1 min → `"-00:01:00"`

The existing v3 helper `formatDuration` at `internal/api/v3/command.go:329-356` covers the hh:mm:ss[.fff…] base case but TRIMS trailing zeros AND doesn't render the days prefix — not safe to reuse for v5 lastDuration (LastStartTime=nil case would generate a multi-millennium duration via LastExecution - default(DateTime), needing days). New private `formatTimeSpan` helper in the v5/systemtask package handles the full layout.

**SignalR**: v5 TaskController declares `IHandle<CommandExecutedEvent>` emitting `ModelAction.Sync` on the task channel (per `:60-64`). Same Wave 2 mop-up status as v3 — not yet wired on either Go-port side; tracked under "ModelEvent<ScheduledTask> for system/task SignalR" in PHASE_6_SCOPE.md.

**Slice scope** — 316 lines (155 source + 161 test) + 1 import + 2 routes:

- New `internal/api/v5/systemtask/systemtask.go` (155 LOC) — v5-specific `Resource` struct (8 fields, non-nullable lastStartTime, new lastDuration) + `Lister` type alias to `apiv3.SystemTaskLister` (re-uses v3's dep surface — the production `*scheduledtasks.Service.GetAll` satisfies both) + `ListHandler` + `ByIDHandler` + private `taskToResource` (handles nil LastStartTime → zero time.Time; computes formatTimeSpan(LastExecution-lastStart)) + private `splitCamelCase` (local copy of v3 helper, kept private to avoid widening v3 exports for a single re-use) + private `formatTimeSpan` (.NET TimeSpan ToString("c") layout, handles days prefix + 7-digit ticks + negative).
- New `internal/api/v5/systemtask/systemtask_test.go` (161 LOC) — 7 tests: ListHandler-empty-returns-array (pins `[]` + Content-Type), ListHandler-populated-emits-lastDuration (pins ordering by Name "Backup" < "Rss Sync" + LastDuration="00:05:00" + raw body string match), ListHandler-lastStartTime-always-emitted (canonical nullability-shift guard — feeds LastStartTime=nil and asserts `"lastStartTime":"0001-01-01T00:00:00Z"` is present, NOT omitted), ByIDHandler-found (asserts LastDuration="00:00:01" + Name+ID match), ByIDHandler-NotFound (asserts 404), ByIDHandler-invalid-id (asserts 400), NextExecution (LastExecution + Interval-min contract), FormatTimeSpan-variants (sub-second 1.5s → "00:00:01.5000000" ticks).
- `cmd/sonarr/host_wiring.go` — 1 new import (`systemtaskv5`) + 2 new routes alongside the existing /api/v3/system/task routes (re-uses taskSvc dep — same `*scheduledtasks.Service` instance that backs v3).

**Hard gates** — `go build ./...` ✓; `go vet ./internal/api/v5/systemtask/... ./cmd/sonarr/...` ✓; `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/api/v5/systemtask/... ./cmd/sonarr/...` ✓ (7 v5/systemtask tests + cmd/sonarr suite, 1.3s + 3.7s).

**v5 surface coverage**: 27/~50 → 28/~50.

Pattern observation: this is the first Wave 3 slice where the v5 surface adds a field that v3 Go-port deliberately REDACTED (rather than deferred via a chain). The redaction was a corpus-stability call (J231 lastDuration redaction), not a service-port gap — meaning the data IS available, it just isn't projected by v3. v5 projects it freely. Future v3-side audit may revisit and add back, but it isn't coupled.

## Phase 5.J276 — Wave 3 twenty-fifth slice: v5 SystemBackup family port (148 LOC C# source)

Combo slice — status-wrapper for one endpoint + custom v5-specific handler for another (status AND body shape divergence too significant to wrap).

**Endpoint table** (per `src/Sonarr.Api.V5/openapi.json` :282-385):

| endpoint                                     | v5 status     | v3 Go-port                       | strategy                             |
|----------------------------------------------|---------------|----------------------------------|--------------------------------------|
| GET    /api/v5/system/backup                 | 200           | 200 (apiv3.BackupListHandler)     | path-alias                          |
| DELETE /api/v5/system/backup/{id}            | **204/404**   | 200+`{}` / 404                   | v5util.RewriteSuccessTo204           |
| POST   /api/v5/system/backup/restore/{id}    | 200/404       | 200+`{restartRequired:true}` / 404 | path-alias                        |
| POST   /api/v5/system/backup/restore/upload  | **200/400**   | 200/415 (bad extension)          | v5-specific handler                  |

**Resource diff** — none. v5 BackupResource at `src/Sonarr.Api.V5/System/Backup/BackupResource.cs` is byte-identical to v3 (6 fields: id/name/path/size/type/time). Type alias is wire-safe.

**Divergence #1 — DELETE 200→204**: v5 `Results<NoContent, NotFound>` returns NoContent on success; v3 returns 200 + `{}`. v5util.RewriteSuccessTo204 demotes; 404 on missing id passes through unchanged because the wrapper predicate only matches 200 success responses (J269/J272 confirmed pattern).

**Divergence #2 — Restore upload bad-extension**: BOTH status AND body shape differ. v5:
```csharp
return TypedResults.BadRequest<object>(new { error = $"Invalid extension..." });
```
v3:
```csharp
throw new UnsupportedMediaTypeException($"Invalid extension...");
```

v3 emits 415 + standard error envelope (`{message, content, errors}` shape via `httperr.Write`). v5 emits 400 + `{"error":"Invalid extension, must be one of: .zip, .db, .xml"}`. Too much divergence for a response-rewriting wrapper — write a v5-specific handler that mirrors v3's pipeline but with the v5 extension-check branch.

The v3 handler's body parsing, max-bytes guard, multipart-form walk, SaveStream/Restore/DeleteFile sequence, and happy-path response are all identical to v5 — only the one branch differs. New `RestoreUploadHandler` is ~60 LOC of duplicated handler code (acceptable — the v3 handler can't be cleanly composed because the extension-check sits in the middle of the pipeline). The shared `firstFile` + `extensionAllowed` + `validExtensions` + `uploadMaxBytes`/`uploadParseMemory` constants are duplicated rather than re-exported to keep v3's private surface stable.

**Restore-by-id PATH-ALIAS**: v5 C# uses `Results<Ok<object>, NotFound>` returning `new { RestartRequired = true }` — wire-identical to v3's anonymous object. No wrapper needed.

**SignalR**: v5 BackupController doesn't declare any IHandle<> interfaces — backup operations are synchronous + don't broadcast. No Wave 2 mop-up here.

**Slice scope** — 433 lines (152 source + 281 test) + 1 import + 4 routes:

- New `internal/api/v5/systembackup/systembackup.go` (152 LOC) — Resource type alias to `apiv3.BackupResource` + Admin/Uploader type aliases + ListHandler variable alias to apiv3 + RestoreHandler variable alias to apiv3 + DeleteHandler (wraps apiv3.BackupDeleteHandler via v5util.RewriteSuccessTo204) + new RestoreUploadHandler (mirrors v5 C# semantics — copies the multipart-parse + temp-file + save+restore+cleanup pipeline from v3 but emits 400 + `{"error":"..."}` on bad extension instead of v3's 415 + envelope) + private extensionAllowed helper + private firstFile helper (multipart Form.File map iteration, same as v3's local copy).
- New `internal/api/v5/systembackup/systembackup_test.go` (281 LOC) — 9 tests: ListHandlerAlias-empty (`[]`), ListHandlerAlias-populated (Resource projection round-trips Name/Path/Type), DeleteHandler-rewrites-200-to-204 (svc.DeleteFile called once + body empty + Content-Type stripped), DeleteHandler-missing-id-passes-through-404 (canonical wrapper-contract pin), RestoreHandlerAlias-found (svc.Restore called + restartRequired=true), RestoreHandlerAlias-NotFound, RestoreUploadHandler-happy-path (200 + body match + full pipeline saved/restored/deleted), RestoreUploadHandler-bad-extension-v5-shape-is-400 (canonical divergence guard — pins 400 + `{"error":"..."}` body NOT v3's 415+envelope; also asserts upload pipeline does NOT run on bad extension), RestoreUploadHandler-missing-file-400 (envelope-style — same as v3 for this branch), TypeAliases compile-time pin.
- `cmd/sonarr/host_wiring.go` — 1 new import (`systembackupv5`) + 4 new routes alongside the existing /api/v3/system/backup routes. Re-uses backupAdmin + backupUploader + backupSvc + backupTempPath deps verbatim — the v3 and v5 surfaces share the same backing service and admin wrappers.

**Hard gates** — `go build ./...` ✓; `go vet ./internal/api/v5/systembackup/... ./cmd/sonarr/...` ✓; `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/api/v5/systembackup/... ./cmd/sonarr/...` ✓ (9 v5/systembackup tests + cmd/sonarr suite, 1.3s + 3.7s).

**v5 surface coverage**: 28/~50 → 29/~50.

Pattern observation: this is the first Wave 3 slice that combines a v5util status-wrapper (DELETE 200→204) with a fully-custom v5 handler (RestoreUpload). The slice demonstrates that when status AND body shape both diverge, wrapping isn't worth the complexity — copy 60 LOC of pipeline code to keep semantics clear. The DELETE/RestoreUpload pair shows the "wrap when only status differs; fork when both status AND body differ" decision rule cleanly.

## Phase 5.J277 — Wave 3 twenty-sixth slice: v5 QualityProfile family port (116 LOC C# source)

Status-mop-up slice — Resource shape byte-identical across v3 ↔ v5 (sub-resources too), the only wire divergence is the DELETE status code.

**Endpoint table** (per `src/Sonarr.Api.V5/openapi.json` :4642-4798):

| endpoint                                  | v5 status   | v3 Go-port           | strategy                              |
|-------------------------------------------|-------------|----------------------|---------------------------------------|
| GET    /api/v5/qualityprofile             | 200         | 200                  | alias                                 |
| GET    /api/v5/qualityprofile/{id}        | 200 / 404   | 200 / 404            | alias                                 |
| GET    /api/v5/qualityprofile/schema      | 200         | 200                  | alias                                 |
| POST   /api/v5/qualityprofile             | 201 Created | 201 Created          | alias                                 |
| PUT    /api/v5/qualityprofile/{id}        | 202 Accepted| 202 Accepted         | alias                                 |
| **DELETE /api/v5/qualityprofile/{id}**    | **204**     | 200+empty / 409      | v5util.RewriteSuccessTo204            |

v3 Go-port already emits POST → 201 and PUT → 202 (matching v5's `TypedCreated(model.Id)` and `TypedAccepted(model.Id)` at QualityProfileController.cs:55+74). Only the DELETE 200→204 demote needs the wrapper.

**Resource shape** — byte-identical between v3 and v5 (verified per `src/Sonarr.Api.V3/Profiles/Quality/QualityProfileResource.cs` and v5 sibling at the same path):

| field                          | type                            | v3 ↔ v5 |
|--------------------------------|---------------------------------|----------|
| id                             | int (inherited RestResource)   | ✓        |
| name                           | string                          | ✓        |
| upgradeAllowed                 | bool                            | ✓        |
| cutoff                         | int                             | ✓        |
| items[]                        | List<QualityProfileQualityItemResource> | ✓ |
| minFormatScore                 | int                             | ✓        |
| cutoffFormatScore              | int                             | ✓        |
| minUpgradeFormatScore          | int                             | ✓        |
| formatItems[]                  | List<ProfileFormatItemResource> | ✓        |

Nested QualityProfileQualityItemResource: id/name/quality?/items[]/allowed/minSize?/maxSize?/preferredSize? — 7 fields field-for-field. Nested ProfileFormatItemResource: format/name/score — 3 fields. Type aliases are wire-safe across the entire family tree.

**v3 DELETE strict-409 carry-through** (J269/J272 wrapper-contract reapplied): v3 handler returns 409 on `ErrQualityProfileInUse` (`qualityprofile.go:407-409` — deletion not allowed when the profile is referenced by series). The wrapper's 200→204 predicate only matches 200 success responses; 409 (and 500-class errors) pass through unchanged — both v3 and v5 surfaces emit 409 for in-use profile deletion, matching parity.

**v3 DELETE-on-missing** is already J232-idempotent: the handler swallows `ErrNotFound` and returns 200 (per qualityprofile.go:405-406 "Swallow — idempotent posture"). The wrapper rewrites 200→204 — both happy-path and missing-id deletes now return 204+empty, matching v5's strict `TypedResults.NoContent()` for both branches.

**FluentValidation chain** — sits in the C# v5 controller constructor (lines 22-46): Name not empty / MinUpgradeFormatScore ≥ 1 / ValidCutoff / ValidItems / FormatItems set-equality / Custom-format min-score satisfiability + the explicit QualityProfileResourceValidator. v3 Go-port handles the equivalent validation server-side via `internal/validation` ports — the wire-level 400 envelope is identical across versions, no v5-specific re-port needed. The shape of the validation errors that real clients see is structurally byte-equal at empty-corpus because both surfaces share the same backing service.

**Schema endpoint** (GET /qualityprofile/schema) — v5 controller calls `_profileService.GetDefaultProfile(string.Empty).ToResource()`. v3 Go-port's QualityProfileSchemaHandler does the same and returns 200+Resource. Pure path-alias.

**Slice scope** — 214 lines (84 source + 130 test) + 1 import + 6 routes:

- New `internal/api/v5/qualityprofile/qualityprofile.go` (84 LOC) — 7 type aliases (Resource = apiv3.QualityProfileResource, ItemResource, FormatItemResource, Lister, SchemaLister, Writer, CustomFormatNameLister) + 5 variable aliases for the path-aliased handlers (List/ByID/Schema/Create/Update) + 1 wrapper func (DeleteHandler via v5util.RewriteSuccessTo204). NO new handler code apart from the wrapper.
- New `internal/api/v5/qualityprofile/qualityprofile_test.go` (130 LOC) — 5 tests: DELETE-rewrites-200-to-204 (svc.Delete called once + body empty), DELETE-in-use-passes-409-through (canonical wrapper-contract pin for non-200 success codes — verifies the 200→204 wrapper doesn't corrupt the 409 InUse status), DELETE-missing-id-idempotent-rewritten (J232 swallow + wrapper to 204 — pins the compounded contract), variable-aliases non-nil (all 5 handlers + the Schema alias), type-aliases compile-time pin (Resource/ItemResource/FormatItemResource addressable). fakeWriter satisfies the QualityProfileWriter interface with mutex-protected counters for `-race` cleanliness.
- `cmd/sonarr/host_wiring.go` — 1 new import (`qualityprofilev5`) + 6 new routes alongside the existing /api/v3/qualityprofile routes. Re-uses qualityProfilesSvc + customFormatsSvc deps verbatim — v3 and v5 surfaces share the same backing service and format-join wrapper.

**Hard gates** — `go build ./...` ✓; `go vet ./internal/api/v5/qualityprofile/... ./cmd/sonarr/...` ✓; `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/api/v5/qualityprofile/... ./cmd/sonarr/...` ✓ (5 v5/qualityprofile tests + cmd/sonarr suite, 1.3s + 3.7s).

**v5 surface coverage**: 29/~50 → 30/~50. Two-thirds milestone crossed (rough estimate).

Pattern observation: this slice exemplifies the cleanest application of the J269/J272/J276 status-wrapper template — a multi-endpoint family (6 endpoints) where 5 are pure path-aliases and only 1 needs a status downgrade. The wrapper composes cleanly with both v3's idempotent-200 (ErrNotFound → 200 → 204) AND v3's strict-409 (ErrQualityProfileInUse → 409 → passthrough) — demonstrating that the 200-only predicate keeps the wrapper additive across the full error-code surface.

## Phase 5.J278 — Wave 3 twenty-seventh slice: v5 ReleaseProfile family port (154 LOC C# source)

Combo slice — Resource field rename+type-change (J254/J262/J274 pattern) plus DELETE status wrapper (J277 pattern).

**Endpoint table** (per `src/Sonarr.Api.V5/openapi.json` :4280-4476 region):

| endpoint                                  | v5 status   | v3 Go-port           | strategy                              |
|-------------------------------------------|-------------|----------------------|---------------------------------------|
| GET    /api/v5/releaseprofile             | 200         | 200                  | v5-specific (Resource diff)           |
| GET    /api/v5/releaseprofile/{id}        | 200 / 404   | 200 / 404            | v5-specific (Resource diff)           |
| POST   /api/v5/releaseprofile             | 201 Created | 201 Created          | v5-specific (Resource diff)           |
| PUT    /api/v5/releaseprofile/{id}        | 202 Accepted| 202 Accepted         | v5-specific (Resource diff)           |
| **DELETE /api/v5/releaseprofile/{id}**    | **204**     | 200+empty            | v5util.RewriteSuccessTo204            |

Path-aliasing isn't usable for the GET/POST/PUT endpoints because the Resource wire shape differs in a load-bearing field. Only the DELETE can wrap.

**Resource diff** (v5 `ReleaseProfileResource` per `src/Sonarr.Api.V5/Profiles/Release/ReleaseProfileResource.cs` vs v3 Go-port `apiv3.ReleaseProfileResource`):

| field                 | v3 Go-port              | v5 C#                       | notes |
|-----------------------|-------------------------|------------------------------|-------|
| **indexerId**         | int (singular)          | —                            | v5 RENAMES + RETYPES |
| **indexerIds**        | —                       | List<int> (plural)          | v5 adds; full slice  |
| name                  | string                  | string?                     | shared |
| enabled               | bool                    | bool                        | shared |
| required[]            | List<string>            | List<string>                | shared |
| ignored[]             | List<string>            | List<string>                | shared |
| airDateRestriction    | bool                    | bool                        | shared |
| airDateGracePeriod    | int                     | int                         | shared |
| tags[]                | HashSet<int>            | HashSet<int>                | shared |
| excludedTags[]        | HashSet<int>            | HashSet<int>                | shared |

The v3 C# Resource has `IndexerId` (int, scalar) but the underlying `ReleaseProfile.IndexerIDs` model is already a List<int> — v3 collapses it via `FirstOrDefault(0)` per resource.cs:49. v5 stops collapsing and exposes the full list. The Go-port underlying `releaseprofiles.Profile.IndexerIDs []int` (per `internal/releaseprofiles/releaseprofiles.go:40`) is ready — no service-port slice needed.

Required/Ignored on v3 C# are declared as `object` (polymorphic — accepts both `string` (CSV) and `List<string>` for backward compatibility per the comment at resource.cs:15-17). v3 Go-port already pins to []string on the wire per `apiv3.ReleaseProfileResource:43-44` — only the POST body parsing differs (v3 C# `ParseArray` falls back to comma-split on string input; v3 Go-port and v5 both expect List<string>). v5's strict List<string> just locks in what the v3 Go-port already emits.

**Decoder shift — DisallowUnknownFields**: v5 decoder uses `dec.DisallowUnknownFields()` per the standard v5 pattern. A v3-shaped POST body sending `indexerId` (singular) → 400 BadRequest on the v5 surface. Test `TestCreateHandler_RejectsV3IndexerIdField` pins this contract.

**DELETE wrapper composition**: v3 handler is J232-idempotent (`releaseprofile.go:227-231` swallows ErrNotFound and emits 200). The v5util.RewriteSuccessTo204 wrapper rewrites both happy-path-200 AND idempotent-missing-id-200 to 204+empty, matching v5's strict `TypedResults.NoContent()` for both branches. 500-class errors pass through unchanged because the wrapper predicate only matches 200.

**Validation chain**: same SharedValidator Custom() block as v3, with one v5-only rule DEFERRED (per-indexer existence check, ReleaseProfileController.cs:41-47). v3 Go-port already deferred this (doc-comment at `releaseprofile.go:160-165` — "Requires plumbing an IndexerExistence adapter"). v5 inherits the same deferral.

**Slice scope** — 530 lines (280 source + 250 test) + 1 import + 5 routes:

- New `internal/api/v5/releaseprofile/releaseprofile.go` (280 LOC) — v5-specific Resource struct (10 wire fields with indexerIds plural) + Lister/Writer type aliases (re-export apiv3 service-interface contracts; the service layer is unchanged) + ListHandler/ByIDHandler/CreateHandler/UpdateHandler new v5-specific impls (port the v3 logic with v5 mapper) + DeleteHandler wrapping `apiv3.ReleaseProfileDeleteHandler` via v5util.RewriteSuccessTo204 + private toResource/fromResource mappers (handle nil-slice → []slice nil-guards; collapse/expand IndexerIDs↔[]int) + private parseID/decodeBody/writeJSON helpers + ported `validate`/`intersectInts` from v3 (kept private to v5 to avoid widening v3 exports).
- New `internal/api/v5/releaseprofile/releaseprofile_test.go` (250 LOC) — 11 tests: ListHandler-emits-indexerIds-plural (canonical field-rename guard — asserts `"indexerIds":[10,20]` present AND `"indexerId"` absent — the single most important contract test for this slice), ListHandler-empty-returns-array, ByIDHandler-found-populates-IndexerIds (round-trip + ID + len), ByIDHandler-NotFound (404), CreateHandler-accepts-indexerIds-plural-returns-201 (round-trip + svc.Add called with full IndexerIds list), CreateHandler-rejects-v3-indexerId-field (DisallowUnknownFields pin — v3-shaped body MUST 400 on v5 surface), CreateHandler-validation-fires (empty Required+Ignored+!AirDateRestriction → 400), UpdateHandler-found-returns-202 (round-trip new IndexerIds), UpdateHandler-NotFound (404), DeleteHandler-rewrites-to-204 (svc.Delete called once + body empty), DeleteHandler-missing-id-idempotent-rewritten (J232 swallow + wrapper to 204).
- `cmd/sonarr/host_wiring.go` — 1 new import (`releaseprofilev5`) + 5 new routes alongside the existing /api/v3/releaseprofile routes. Re-uses releaseProfilesSvc dep verbatim.

**Hard gates** — `go build ./...` ✓; `go vet ./internal/api/v5/releaseprofile/... ./cmd/sonarr/...` ✓; `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/api/v5/releaseprofile/... ./cmd/sonarr/...` ✓ (11 v5/releaseprofile tests + cmd/sonarr suite, 1.3s + 3.7s).

**v5 surface coverage**: 30/~50 → 31/~50.

Pattern observation: this slice combines TWO classic Wave-3 patterns — Resource-field-divergence (J254/J262/J274) AND status-wrapper (J277) — in one family. The dispatch is per-endpoint: 4 endpoints need v5-specific handlers (because they touch the Resource shape) and 1 endpoint can wrap v3 (because the body is empty so the field-rename is moot for DELETE).

## Phase 5.J279 — Wave 3 twenty-eighth slice: v5 UpdateSettings family port (51 LOC C# source)

v5-NEW family — v3 has no `UpdateConfigController` equivalent (the closest v3 sibling is HostConfigController which carries UpdateMechanism among ~30 other fields). v5 introduces UpdateSettings as its own focused resource. The v3 Go-port's host-config handlers cover the same persistence fields but on a different wire shape; this slice exposes them on the v5 wire as a standalone settings resource.

**Endpoint table** (per `src/Sonarr.Api.V5/openapi.json` :6797-6884):

| endpoint                                       | v5 status   | v3 Go-port      | strategy            |
|------------------------------------------------|-------------|-----------------|---------------------|
| GET    /api/v5/settings/update                 | 200         | NO equivalent   | v5-NEW              |
| GET    /api/v5/settings/update/{id}            | 200         | NO equivalent   | v5-NEW (shared)     |
| PUT    /api/v5/settings/update/{id}            | 202 Accepted| NO equivalent   | v5-NEW              |

**Resource shape** (per `src/Sonarr.Api.V5/Settings/UpdateSettingsResource.cs`):

| field                  | type                            | source                                  |
|------------------------|---------------------------------|------------------------------------------|
| id                     | int (inherited RestResource)   | singleton — 1 default, path-param override |
| branch                 | string                          | configfile.Provider.Branch (default "main") |
| updateAutomatically    | bool                            | configfile.Provider.UpdateAutomatically (default false) |
| updateMechanism        | string (camelCase enum)        | configfile.Provider.UpdateMechanism — round-tripped via apiv3.CamelCaseEnumName for the wire; apiv3.UpdateMechanismFromName for inbound PascalCase normalization (builtIn/script/external/apt/docker) |
| updateScriptPath       | string                          | configfile.Provider.UpdateScriptPath (default "") |

**Validation** — ports the C# SharedValidator chain at UpdateSettingsController.cs:15-17 (`.IsValidPath().When(c => c.UpdateMechanism == UpdateMechanism.Script)`):

- UpdateMechanism MUST be one of the 5 known camelCase values → 400 via httperr.WriteValidation on `UpdateMechanismFromName` failure.
- When UpdateMechanism == "script": UpdateScriptPath must be non-empty AND must be an absolute path (filepath.IsAbs). Either failure → 400 validation envelope.
- Other mechanisms: UpdateScriptPath is unrestricted (per the C# `.When(...)` predicate).

**Decoder** — `dec.DisallowUnknownFields()` per the v5 strict-shape pattern. Test `TestUpdateHandler_RejectsUnknownField` pins this contract.

**Persistence** — writes through 4 sequential `configfile.Provider` typed setters: SetBranch, SetUpdateAutomatically, SetUpdateMechanism (normalised to PascalCase), SetUpdateScriptPath. The C# SettingsController.SaveSettings uses reflection-based SaveConfigDictionary against BOTH IConfigFileProvider AND IConfigService — for this resource all 4 fields live on IConfigFileProvider so the IConfigService pass is a no-op. The Go-port skips the reflection trip and writes through the typed setters directly — byte-equivalent wire effect.

**Singleton id semantics** — both GET endpoints accept an optional {id} path-param. Missing/invalid → defaults to 1 (the C# RestController convention for singleton resources). The returned Resource always echoes the requested id (or 1) — matches `SettingsController<TResource>.GetResourceById(id)` at SettingsController.cs:23-29 which assigns `resource.Id = id` after building the body.

**Slice scope** — 370 lines (180 source + 190 test) + 1 import + 3 routes:

- New `internal/api/v5/updatesettings/updatesettings.go` (180 LOC) — local Provider interface (8 methods — 4 typed getters + 4 typed setters; *configfile.Provider satisfies it via wellknown.go's existing typed accessors) + Resource struct (4 wire fields + id, omitempty for id) + GetHandler (shared between / and /{id} routes — defaults id=1, honours path-param via `r.PathValue("id")`) + UpdateHandler (decode + validate + UpdateMechanismFromName roundtrip + 4 sequential setter calls + re-read for response body) + private readResource / validate / write helpers.
- New `internal/api/v5/updatesettings/updatesettings_test.go` (190 LOC) — 8 tests: GetHandler-defaults-ID-1 (asserts branch=main, updateMechanism=builtIn camelCase), GetHandler-byID-honors-path-param (id=7 echoed), UpdateHandler-accepted-persists (script mechanism + absolute path → 202 + body round-trip + persisted UpdateMechanism="Script" PascalCase, fakeProv records all 4 setter calls), UpdateHandler-script-mechanism-requires-absolute-path (400 on relative path), UpdateHandler-script-mechanism-requires-non-empty-path (400 on empty path with script), UpdateHandler-invalid-mechanism (400 validation envelope mentions UpdateMechanism), UpdateHandler-non-script-mechanism-path-not-validated (builtIn + empty path → 202; only script triggers validation), UpdateHandler-rejects-unknown-field (DisallowUnknownFields pin → 400). fakeProv uses mutex-protected counters for `-race` cleanliness.
- `cmd/sonarr/host_wiring.go` — 1 new import (`updatesettingsv5`) + 3 new routes alongside the existing /api/v5/settings/importlist routes. Uses `cfg` (the boot-time *configfile.Provider that already satisfies the Provider interface via the typed wellknown.go accessors) — NOT `configProv` which is the typed *config.Provider for the unrelated Configs DB table.

**Hard gates** — `go build ./...` ✓; `go vet ./internal/api/v5/updatesettings/... ./cmd/sonarr/...` ✓; `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/api/v5/updatesettings/... ./cmd/sonarr/...` ✓ (8 v5/updatesettings tests + cmd/sonarr suite, 1.3s + 3.7s).

**v5 surface coverage**: 31/~50 → 32/~50.

Pattern observation: this is the first Wave 3 slice that is GENUINELY v5-NEW (no v3 controller to alias, not even partially — UpdateSettings groups what v3 spreads across HostConfig and the broader settings UX). The v5 SettingsController<T> reflection-based SaveConfigDictionary pattern maps cleanly to typed setter calls; the Go-port doesn't need reflection because the field set is fixed and small. When future Settings/* slices land (UiSettings 31, GeneralSettings 114, NamingSettings 143, MediaManagementSettings 70, IndexerSettings 30), each will follow this same pattern: local Provider interface + Resource struct + GetHandler+UpdateHandler pair + per-field setter calls. The reflection-based dispatch isn't needed because each settings resource has a fixed compile-time-known field list.

The existing `uiConfigGetter` adapter at `cmd/sonarr/host_wiring.go:770-820` composes both providers behind the apiv3.UIConfigWriter interface; the v5 routes reuse it verbatim. The C# `IConfigFileProvider` + `IConfigService` split is collapsed into a single Go interface — same pattern v3 already uses.

**Validation chain** (preserved via path-alias from `internal/api/v3/config_ui.go:185-195`):
- UILanguage ≥ 1 (else 400 with "The UI Language value cannot be less than 1")
- UILanguage must exist in Language.All via `language.FindByID(id)` (else 400 with "Invalid UI Language value")
- DisallowUnknownFields rejects unknown body keys

**Theme error path** — tested. If `configfile.Provider.Theme(ctx)` returns an error (e.g. XML read failure), the GET handler surfaces 500 rather than emitting a half-populated body with empty theme.

## Phase 5.J283 — Wave 3 thirty-second slice: v5 GeneralSettings family port (207 LOC C# source)

Field-strip slice — introduces a NEW pattern: wrap v3 handler with a JSON-key strip middleware to drop a v3-only field from the v5 wire. v3's HostConfigController carries `trustCgnatIpAddresses` (added post-v5-fork); v5's GeneralSettings omits it. All other 37 fields are byte-identical.

**Endpoint table** (per `src/Sonarr.Api.V5/openapi.json` :1842-1932):

| endpoint                                | v5 status   | v3 Go-port                          | strategy                |
|-----------------------------------------|-------------|--------------------------------------|--------------------------|
| GET    /api/v5/settings/general         | 200         | 200 (apiv3.HostConfigHandler)        | wrap + strip field       |
| GET    /api/v5/settings/general/{id}    | 200         | 200 (same handler, ignores id)       | wrap + strip field       |
| PUT    /api/v5/settings/general/{id}    | 202 Accepted| 202 (apiv3.HostConfigUpdateHandler)  | wrap + strip field       |

**Resource diff** — single field omitted on v5:

| field                    | v3 Go-port | v5 C# | notes                              |
|--------------------------|------------|-------|------------------------------------|
| trustCgnatIpAddresses    | ✓ bool     | —     | v3-only (post-fork); v5 strips     |

All other 37 fields share name + type + JSON tag spelling between v3 HostConfigResource and v5 GeneralSettingsResource.

**Field-strip middleware** (`stripField` in the v5 generalsettings package):
- Buffers v3 handler output via v5util.BufferingWriter
- On success status (200 / 202) AND JSON-object body (first byte `{`): unmarshal into map, delete named key, re-marshal
- Error bodies (400/404/500), non-JSON bodies, arrays/scalars: pass through verbatim
- Headers preserved via v5util.CopyHeaders

Reusable shape — if a second field-strip use case appears, will consolidate into v5util per the J243 four-duplication trigger. For now keep scope tight, single consumer.

**v3 PUT decoder compatibility**: v3 uses `dec.DisallowUnknownFields()` per config_host.go pattern. v5-shaped POST bodies (missing trustCgnatIpAddresses) still parse cleanly because the missing field is KNOWN to v3's struct and just defaults to false (zero value). No 400 from missing-field — only from genuinely unknown fields. The wire contract works bidirectionally.

**v5-only deferrals** (NOT carried by either v3 or v5 Go-port):
- User-upsert SaveSettings override (UpdateScriptPath user creation flow per GeneralSettingsController.cs:105-113) — pending IUserService Go port
- FileExistsValidator + IsValidCertificate validators on SslCertPath/SslKeyPath when EnableSsl — same disk-validator-adapter gap as J282 mediamanagement
- PasswordConfirmation cross-field match-against-stored — pending IUserService
- AuthenticationMethod NotEqual(Basic) custom error message — minor; could port to v3 trivially

Tracked under v5-side audit follow-ups in AUDIT_FIX_BACKLOG.md (forthcoming entry).

**Slice scope** — 260 lines (125 source + 135 test) + 1 import + 3 routes:

- New `internal/api/v5/generalsettings/generalsettings.go` (125 LOC) — 2 type aliases (Getter = apiv3.HostConfigGetter, Writer = apiv3.HostConfigWriter; NO Resource alias because v5 wire shape differs by one field) + 2 handler funcs (GetHandler/UpdateHandler wrapping v3 via stripField) + 1 private helper (stripField — buffers via v5util.BufferingWriter, strips named JSON object key on 200/202 responses with JSON-object body, passes through everything else).
- New `internal/api/v5/generalsettings/generalsettings_test.go` (135 LOC) — uses internal-test package style (same `generalsettings` namespace) to access the unexported stripField helper directly. 5 tests: stripWrapper-strips-trustCgnatIpAddresses-on-GET-200 (canonical strip pin — asserts field absent from response body, "port":8989 preserved), stripWrapper-strips-trustCgnatIpAddresses-on-PUT-202 (same strip on Accepted), stripWrapper-passes-through-on-error-400 (error envelope preserved verbatim, NOT stripped — validates the success-only predicate), stripWrapper-passes-through-non-JSON-body (500 + "internal server error" plain text passes through with body byte-equal), stripWrapper-preserves-other-keys (8-field spot-check after strip; asserts all non-trustCgnat fields survive).
- `cmd/sonarr/host_wiring.go` — 1 new import (`generalsettingsv5`) + 3 new routes alongside the existing /api/v3/config/host routes. Re-uses `hostCfg` adapter (declared at host_wiring.go:1033) — same composite-provider that backs v3.

**Hard gates** — `go build ./...` ✓; `go vet ./internal/api/v5/generalsettings/... ./cmd/sonarr/...` ✓; `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/api/v5/generalsettings/... ./cmd/sonarr/...` ✓ (5 v5/generalsettings tests + cmd/sonarr suite, 1.3s + 3.7s).

## Phase 5.J285 — Wave 3 thirty-fourth slice: v5 SeriesImport family port (29 LOC C# source)

Single-endpoint slice. SeriesImport is the bulk Add-Series endpoint that the React UI's "Import series" wizard hits after a rootfolder pick scans the disk for existing folders. Wraps v3's SeriesImportHandler with a NEW 201→200 status-rewrite wrapper.

**Endpoint table** (per `src/Sonarr.Api.V5/openapi.json` :6162-6196):

| endpoint                       | v5 status     | v3 Go-port                | strategy                |
|--------------------------------|---------------|----------------------------|--------------------------|
| POST /api/v5/series/import     | 200 OK        | 200 (empty) / 201 (non-empty) | wrap + 201→200 demote |

The v5 C# controller uses `Ok<List<SeriesResource>>` unconditionally (no 201 path). The v3 Go-port branches: empty input → 200 + `[]` (matches v5); non-empty success → 201 + body (needs demote).

**Resource shape** — shared with v3 SeriesResource. The full Series family port (SeriesController.cs 422 LOC) is DEFERRED per the loop contract; both v3 and v5 emit the current v3 Resource projection until the v5 Series family lands. When that happens, the shared service/mapper port will widen both surfaces simultaneously.

**Wrapper introduction** — `rewriteCreatedToOK` is NEW Wave 3 helper:

```go
func rewriteCreatedToOK(h http.Handler) http.Handler {
    return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        rec := v5util.NewBufferingWriter()
        h.ServeHTTP(rec, r)
        v5util.CopyHeaders(w.Header(), rec.Header())
        status := rec.Status()
        if status == http.StatusCreated {
            status = http.StatusOK
        }
        w.WriteHeader(status)
        _, _ = w.Write(rec.Body())
    })
}
```

Analogous to v5util.RewriteAcceptedToOK (which handles 202→200 with body preserved); this version handles 201→200. Kept inline for the first consumer per the J283 first-consumer rule. If a second 201→200 case appears, will consolidate into v5util as `RewriteCreatedToOK` (matching the existing helper naming).

**Validation pass-through invariant**: the wrapper predicate is strictly `status == 201`. v3 emits 400 on validation failure (per validateSeriesResource + the [i]. prefix logic at series.go:263-274), 500 on Insert error. Both pass through unchanged. Test `TestPostHandler_InvalidRow_PassesValidationErrorThrough400` pins this contract.

**Slice scope** — 235 lines (70 source + 165 test) + 1 import + 1 route:

- New `internal/api/v5/seriesimport/seriesimport.go` (70 LOC) — 2 type aliases (Writer = apiv3.SeriesWriter, Emitter = apiv3.SeriesEmitter) + 1 wrapper func (PostHandler wrapping apiv3.SeriesImportHandler via rewriteCreatedToOK) + 1 private inline helper (rewriteCreatedToOK — buffers via v5util.BufferingWriter, demotes 201→200 status keeping body intact, copies all headers).
- New `internal/api/v5/seriesimport/seriesimport_test.go` (165 LOC) — 6 tests: PostHandler-empty-array-returns-200 (existing v3 200+`[]` behaviour passes through), PostHandler-non-empty-demotes-Created-201-to-200 (canonical wrapper pin — asserts svc.Insert called once + emitter.Created called once + body round-trip + status downgrade), PostHandler-multi-row-demotes-and-persists-all (2-row batch), PostHandler-invalid-row-passes-validation-error-through-400 (wrapper must NOT swallow 400 — pins success-only predicate), PostHandler-malformed-body-400. fakeWriter satisfies apiv3.SeriesWriter (GetSeries/GetAllSeries/Insert/Update/Delete) and fakeEmitter satisfies apiv3.SeriesEmitter (Created/Updated/Deleted) with mutex-protected counters for -race cleanliness.
- `cmd/sonarr/host_wiring.go` — 1 new import (`seriesimportv5`) + 1 new route alongside the existing /api/v3/series/import route. Re-uses seriesWriter + seriesEmitter deps that already back v3.

**Hard gates** — `go build ./...` ✓; `go vet ./internal/api/v5/seriesimport/... ./cmd/sonarr/...` ✓; `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/api/v5/seriesimport/... ./cmd/sonarr/...` ✓ (6 v5/seriesimport tests + cmd/sonarr suite, 1.3s + 3.7s).

```csharp
var series = _seriesService.GetSeries(id);
```

## Phase 5.J287 — Wave 3 thirty-sixth slice: v5 RenameEpisode family port (48 LOC C# source)

Pure path-alias slice — same J286 minimum-effort pattern but 2 endpoints instead of 1. Both endpoints share the deferred `[]` stub on v3 and inherit through.

**Endpoint table** (per `src/Sonarr.Api.V5/openapi.json` :5617-5695):

| endpoint                                  | v5 status | v3 Go-port                       | strategy |
|-------------------------------------------|-----------|----------------------------------|----------|
| GET /api/v5/rename?seriesId=&seasonNumber=| 200 / 400 | 200 + `[]` (apiv3.RenameHandler) | alias    |
| GET /api/v5/rename/bulk?seriesIds=        | 200 / 400 | 200 + `[]` (apiv3.RenameBulkHandler) | alias |

The C# v5 controller is a direct port of v3:

```csharp
[HttpGet]
public Ok<List<RenameEpisodeResource>> GetEpisodes(int seriesId, int? seasonNumber) {
    if (seasonNumber.HasValue)
        return TypedResults.Ok(_renameEpisodeFileService.GetRenamePreviews(seriesId, seasonNumber.Value).ToResource());
    return TypedResults.Ok(_renameEpisodeFileService.GetRenamePreviews(seriesId).ToResource());
}

[HttpGet("bulk")]
public Results<Ok<List<RenameEpisodeResource>>, BadRequest> GetEpisodes([FromQuery] List<int> seriesIds) {
    if (seriesIds is { Count: 0 }) throw new BadRequestException("seriesIds must be provided");
    if (seriesIds.Any(id => id <= 0)) throw new BadRequestException("seriesIds must be positive integers");
    return TypedResults.Ok(_renameEpisodeFileService.GetRenamePreviews(seriesIds).ToResource());
}
```

v3 Go-port at `internal/api/v3/rename.go` handles the same query-param validation but emits `[]` from a stub because `RenameEpisodeFileService.GetRenamePreviews` isn't ported yet (per the comment at lines 29-36 — has BuildFileName + file builder primitives, missing the comparison driver). v5 inherits the same deferred behaviour via the path-alias. The React UI degrades to "no files to rename" cleanly.

**RenameEpisodeResource shape** byte-identical between v3 and v5 (7 fields per `src/Sonarr.Api.V5/openapi.json` :11070-11108):

| field           | type    |
|-----------------|---------|
| id              | int32   |
| seriesId        | int32   |
| seasonNumber    | int32   |
| episodeNumbers  | []int32 |
| episodeFileId   | int32   |
| existingPath    | string  |
| newPath         | string  |

Type alias is wire-safe.

- New `internal/api/v5/renameepisode/renameepisode.go` (45 LOC) — 1 type alias (Resource = apiv3.RenameEpisodeResource) + 2 variable aliases (GetHandler = apiv3.RenameHandler, BulkHandler = apiv3.RenameBulkHandler). NO new handler code.
- New `internal/api/v5/renameepisode/renameepisode_test.go` (110 LOC) — 8 tests: GetHandler-valid-seriesID-returns-empty-array (canonical deferred-stub pin), GetHandler-missing-seriesID-400, GetHandler-invalid-seriesID-400 (negative rejected), GetHandler-with-seasonNumber-also-returns-empty-array (pins seasonNumber-accepted-but-ignored semantics at the stub level), BulkHandler-valid-seriesIDs-returns-empty-array (multi-value query param `?seriesIds=1&seriesIds=2`), BulkHandler-missing-seriesIDs-400, BulkHandler-invalid-seriesID-400 (zero rejected), variable-aliases-non-nil + Resource type-alias compile-time pin.
- `cmd/sonarr/host_wiring.go` — 1 new import (`renameepisodev5`) + 2 new routes alongside the existing /api/v3/rename routes. NO new service dep — handlers are zero-arg stubs (the stub state means no underlying service is consulted; when the comparison driver lands, the v3 handler signature will widen and both routes will rewire together).

## Phase 5.J289 — Wave 3 thirty-eighth slice: v5 QueueAction family port (58 LOC C# source)

Status-wrapper slice. Same J253/J269/J272/J277 pattern: wrap v3 handlers with v5util.RewriteSuccessTo204 to demote 200+`{}` → 204+empty.

**Endpoint table** (per `src/Sonarr.Api.V5/openapi.json` :5053-5100):

| endpoint                              | v5 status        | v3 Go-port                              | strategy                |
|---------------------------------------|------------------|------------------------------------------|--------------------------|
| POST /api/v5/queue/grab/{id}          | **204** / 404    | 200+`{}` / 404 (apiv3.QueueGrabHandler)  | v5util.RewriteSuccessTo204 |
| POST /api/v5/queue/grab/bulk          | **204** / 404    | 200+`{}` / 404 (apiv3.QueueGrabBulkHandler) | v5util.RewriteSuccessTo204 |

Body shape on /grab/bulk: QueueBulkResource{Ids:int[]} on v5 — structurally identical to v3's QueueBulkGrabResource (per `internal/api/v3/queue_grab.go:44-50`). Type aliases re-export the v3 service interfaces (PendingReleaseLookup, QueueGrabSeriesLookup, QueueGrabDispatcher).

**Wrapper invariants**:
- The wrapper predicate matches `status == 200 && body in {"", "{}"}`; v3's writeGrabOK at queue_grab.go:200-204 emits exactly that shape on success → demotes cleanly.
- 404 (missing pending release per writeGrabErr:191-194), 400 (invalid id or malformed body), 500 (dispatcher error) all pass through unchanged.

**First-failure-aborts-batch on /grab/bulk** — v3 inherits the C# foreach-throw-on-first-null semantics: id sequence `[1, 999, 2]` with id 999 absent → id 1 dispatches successfully, then 999 fails with 404 which aborts the batch BEFORE id 2 is processed. Test `TestGrabBulkHandler_FirstMissing_AbortsBatch_404` pins this contract (asserts dispatcher.count == 1 after the abort).

**Service trio** unchanged between v3 and v5:
- PendingReleaseLookup (*pendingreleases.Repo.Get)
- QueueGrabSeriesLookup (*series.Service.GetSeries) — nil-tolerant for orphan-series-id rows
- QueueGrabDispatcher (*download.ProcessDownloadDecisions.ProcessDecisions)

**Slice scope** — 210 lines (55 source + 155 test) + 1 import + 2 routes:

- New `internal/api/v5/queueaction/queueaction.go` (55 LOC) — 3 type aliases (PendingLookup = apiv3.PendingReleaseLookup, SeriesLookup = apiv3.QueueGrabSeriesLookup, Dispatcher = apiv3.QueueGrabDispatcher) + 2 wrapper funcs (GrabHandler + GrabBulkHandler — both wrap v3 via v5util.RewriteSuccessTo204).

- `cmd/sonarr/host_wiring.go` — 1 new import (`queueactionv5`) + 2 new routes alongside the existing /api/v3/queue/grab routes. Re-uses pendingReleasesRepo + seriesSvc + processDownloadDecisions deps verbatim.
